questions.questionEn: According to the BC Patient Assessment Model, which sequence correctly lists the seven components in their standard order?
questions.questionZh: 按照 BC 病人评估模型（Patient Assessment Model），下列哪一项按标准顺序正确列出了全部七个组成部分？

options.en: Primary Survey, Rescue Scene Evaluation, Secondary Survey, Treatments, Protocols, Load and Transport, Records and Reports
options.zh: 初级评估、现场救援评估、二级评估、处置、协议、装载转运、记录与报告

options.en: Rescue Scene Evaluation, Primary Survey, Secondary Survey, Protocols, Treatments, Load and Transport, Records and Reports
options.zh: 现场救援评估、初级评估、二级评估、协议、处置、装载转运、记录与报告

options.en: Rescue Scene Evaluation, Secondary Survey, Primary Survey, Protocols, Treatments, Records and Reports, Load and Transport
options.zh: 现场救援评估、二级评估、初级评估、协议、处置、记录与报告、装载转运

options.en: Primary Survey, Secondary Survey, Rescue Scene Evaluation, Load and Transport, Protocols, Treatments, Records and Reports
options.zh: 初级评估、二级评估、现场救援评估、装载转运、协议、处置、记录与报告

questions.explanationEn: The model diagram on p.6 runs: Rescue Scene Evaluation, Primary Survey, Secondary Survey, Protocols, Treatments, Load and Transport, Records and Reports. A and D are wrong because they start with the primary survey - the scene must be evaluated for hazards before anyone approaches the patient. C is wrong because the primary survey (life threats) always comes before the secondary survey, and records and reports close the call rather than coming before transport. The footnote allows load and transport to move earlier for unstable patients, and the component table on p.9 notes that the sequence may vary with the call, but this is the generic order.
questions.explanationZh: 第 6 页的模型图顺序是：现场救援评估（Rescue Scene Evaluation）→ 初级评估（Primary Survey）→ 二级评估（Secondary Survey）→ 协议（Protocols）→ 处置（Treatments）→ 装载转运（Load and Transport）→ 记录与报告（Records and Reports）。A 和 D 错在以初级评估开头——必须先评估现场有无危险，才能接近病人。C 错在把二级评估放到初级评估之前（危及生命的问题必须先处理），还把记录与报告放在转运之前，而记录报告应是整个出车的收尾。脚注允许不稳定病人提前装载转运，第 9 页的组成表也说明顺序可随现场情况调整，但通用顺序如上。

questions.questionEn: You arrive at a single-vehicle MVA at night. The car has struck a power pole and a wire is draped across the hood. The driver is slumped over the wheel. What should you do first?
questions.questionZh: 夜间你到达一起单车事故现场：汽车撞上电线杆，一根电线搭在引擎盖上，驾驶员趴在方向盘上。你首先应该做什么？

options.en: Approach the driver's window and begin the primary survey through the glass
options.zh: 走到驾驶座车窗旁，隔着车窗开始初级评估

options.en: Tell the driver to open the door and step out of the vehicle
options.zh: 让驾驶员自己打开车门下车

options.en: Stage at a safe distance until the utility crew confirms the line is dead
options.zh: 在安全距离外待命，直到电力公司确认电线已断电

options.en: Lift the wire off the hood with a dry wooden pole to reach the patient
options.zh: 用干燥的木杆把电线从引擎盖上挑开，以便接触病人

questions.explanationEn: Hazards are the first step of the Rescue Scene Evaluation, and the BC electrical contact guideline is explicit: do not approach electrical sources or downed power lines until qualified personnel have deemed the scene safe. A puts you within reach of an energized vehicle. B is dangerous because stepping out can complete a circuit between the car and the ground - occupants should stay inside until the power is cut. D is wrong because only the utility crew can make the line safe; a 'dry' pole is not reliable insulation against high voltage. Once the line is confirmed dead, begin the primary survey.
questions.explanationZh: 危险评估（Hazards）是现场救援评估的第一步，BC 电击伤（Electrical Contact）指南也写得很清楚：在合格人员确认现场安全之前，不得接近电源或落地电线。A 会让你进入带电车辆的范围。B 很危险：下车时人体可能在车身和地面之间形成回路，断电前车内人员应留在车内。D 错在只有电力公司才能让电线变安全，所谓「干燥」的木杆并不能可靠地隔绝高压电。确认断电后再开始初级评估。

questions.questionEn: What is the stated purpose of the primary survey in the BC Patient Assessment Model?
questions.questionZh: 在 BC 病人评估模型中，初级评估（primary survey）的既定目的是什么？

options.en: To identify and manage life- and limb-threatening injuries and conditions
options.zh: 识别并处理危及生命和肢体的损伤与病情

options.en: To establish a baseline set of vital signs and identify the chief complaint
options.zh: 建立一组基线生命体征并明确主诉

options.en: To ensure the scene is safe for the crew and the patient
options.zh: 确保现场对救护人员和病人都安全

options.en: To gather a complete SAMPLE history before treatment begins
options.zh: 在开始处置前采集完整的 SAMPLE 病史

questions.explanationEn: The component table on p.9 states the purpose of the primary survey: to identify and manage life- and limb-threatening injuries and conditions. B is the stated purpose of the secondary survey (chief complaint, baseline vital signs). C is the purpose of the Rescue Scene Evaluation. D is wrong because a SAMPLE history belongs to the history step of the secondary survey, and management of life threats must not wait for it.
questions.explanationZh: 第 9 页的组成表写明初级评估的目的：识别并处理危及生命和肢体的损伤与病情。B 是二级评估的目的（明确主诉、建立基线生命体征）。C 是现场救援评估的目的。D 错在 SAMPLE 病史属于二级评估中的病史采集，处理危及生命的问题不能等病史问完再做。

questions.questionEn: Which element of the secondary survey is specifically listed in the BC guidelines as required at the PCP level?
questions.questionZh: BC 考纲中，二级评估（secondary survey）的哪一项被特别注明为 PCP 必做（PCP required）？

options.en: Head-to-toe examination
options.zh: 从头到脚检查（head-to-toe examination）

options.en: Baseline vital signs
options.zh: 基线生命体征

options.en: History taking
options.zh: 病史采集（history）

options.en: Functional inquiry
options.zh: 系统问诊（functional inquiry）

questions.explanationEn: The secondary survey consists of history, vital signs, head-to-toe examination, and functional inquiry, and only functional inquiry is annotated 'PCP required'. History, vital signs, and the head-to-toe examination are expected at all licence levels, so A, B, and C are not the item singled out for PCPs.
questions.explanationZh: 二级评估包括病史、生命体征、从头到脚检查和系统问诊（functional inquiry），其中只有系统问诊注明「PCP required」。病史、生命体征和从头到脚检查是所有执照级别都要做的，所以 A、B、C 都不是专门标给 PCP 的那一项。

questions.questionEn: A 24-year-old man has been stabbed in the left chest. Your primary survey finds respiratory distress with accessory muscle use, and you have sealed an open chest wound. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.questionZh: 一名 24 岁男子左胸被刺伤。初级评估发现他呼吸窘迫、辅助呼吸肌参与呼吸，你已封闭了胸部开放伤口。下一步最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Complete a full head-to-toe examination on scene before moving him
options.zh: 搬动前先在现场完成完整的从头到脚检查

options.en: Load and begin transport now, completing the secondary survey en route
options.zh: 立即装载并开始转运，二级评估在途中完成

options.en: Obtain a SAMPLE history and a second set of vital signs before moving him
options.zh: 搬动前先问完 SAMPLE 病史并测第二组生命体征

options.en: Remain on scene and wait for an ALS intercept before moving him
options.zh: 留在现场，等高级生命支持（ALS）赶到后再搬动

questions.explanationEn: Respiratory distress with accessory muscle use and major penetrating torso trauma are both BC instability criteria (p.7). The model's footnote (p.6) allows load and transport any time after the decision point when the patient is unstable, so the secondary survey continues en route. A and C spend on-scene time on secondary-survey steps that do not change his need for definitive care. D is wrong because waiting for an intercept delays transport; if more help is wanted, arrange to meet it en route rather than holding the patient on scene.
questions.explanationZh: 呼吸窘迫伴辅助呼吸肌参与、躯干大穿透伤都属于 BC 不稳定标准（第 7 页）。模型脚注（第 6 页）规定，不稳定病人在决策点之后即可装载转运，二级评估在途中继续。A 和 C 把现场时间花在二级评估的步骤上，并不能改变他需要确定性治疗的事实。D 错在原地等高级生命支持会延误转运；如需支援，应在途中安排会合，而不是把病人留在现场。

questions.questionEn: You find a 30-year-old man lying on a couch after a party. He does not respond when you enter, but when you loudly call his name he opens his eyes, mumbles an answer, and drifts back off. On the AVPU scale he is:
questions.questionZh: 聚会结束后，你发现一名 30 岁男子躺在沙发上。你进门时他毫无反应，但你大声叫他名字时，他睁开眼、含糊地应了一句，随即又昏睡过去。按 AVPU 评估，他属于：

options.en: V - he responds to your voice but is drowsy
options.zh: V——对声音有反应，但嗜睡

options.en: A - he is alert because he answered when spoken to
options.zh: A——别人叫他时他回答了，所以属于清醒

options.en: P - a loud voice counts as a painful stimulus
options.zh: P——大声喊叫算作疼痛刺激

options.en: U - he is unresponsive because he keeps drifting off
options.zh: U——他一直昏睡，属于无反应

questions.explanationEn: BC's AVPU table (p.13) defines V as a patient who responds to verbal stimulus but is drowsy; such a patient may be placed semi-prone if injuries permit. B is wrong because 'alert' means awake and talking without prompting - he did not respond until called loudly. C is wrong because a loud voice is still a verbal stimulus; P requires a physical painful stimulus. D is wrong because he did respond to voice; U means no response to any stimulus.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的 AVPU 表（第 13 页）把「对言语刺激有反应但嗜睡」定义为 V，此类病人如损伤允许可考虑侧俯卧位（semi-prone）。B 错：A（alert）指病人清醒、能自主交谈，而他要大声叫名字才有反应。C 错：再大声也是言语刺激，P 需要的是身体上的疼痛刺激。D 错：他对声音有反应，U 指对任何刺激都没有反应。

questions.questionEn: A warehouse worker is found unconscious on the floor at the base of a storage rack. Nobody saw what happened. There are no obvious injuries. Regarding cervical spine stabilization, you should:
questions.questionZh: 一名仓库工人被发现昏迷倒在货架底下的地面上，无人目击经过，身上没有明显外伤。关于颈椎固定，你应该：

options.en: Defer spinal precautions because there are no visible injuries above the clavicles
options.zh: 锁骨以上看不到损伤，暂不做脊柱保护

options.en: Withhold spinal precautions until he wakes and can report neck pain
options.zh: 等他醒来能说出有无颈痛后再决定是否做脊柱保护

options.en: Apply the NEXUS criteria now to decide whether precautions are needed
options.zh: 现在就用 NEXUS 标准判断是否需要保护

options.en: Stabilize the c-spine, since he is unconscious and trauma cannot be ruled out
options.zh: 进行颈椎固定，因为他昏迷且无法排除外伤

questions.explanationEn: BC lists three indications for cervical spine stabilization in the primary survey (p.11): meets NEXUS or Canadian C-Spine criteria, obvious injury above the clavicles, or an unconscious patient in whom trauma cannot reasonably be ruled out. An unwitnessed collapse at the foot of a storage rack could involve a fall or a falling object, so the third indication applies. A is wrong because the absence of visible injury does not remove that indication. B is wrong because you cannot wait for a symptom an unconscious patient cannot report. C is wrong because NEXUS requires an alert patient who can be examined; an unconscious patient cannot be cleared with it.
questions.explanationZh: BC 列出初级评估中颈椎固定的三条指征（第 11 页）：符合 NEXUS 或加拿大颈椎规则（Canadian C-Spine）、锁骨以上有明显损伤、昏迷且无法合理排除外伤。货架底下无人目击的倒地可能是坠落或被重物砸到，符合第三条。A 错：看不到外伤并不能取消这条指征。B 错：不能等一个昏迷病人根本无法说出的症状。C 错：NEXUS 只适用于意识清楚、能配合检查的病人，昏迷病人无法据此排除颈椎损伤。

questions.questionEn: During the rapid body survey of a stabbing victim you discover a bubbling open wound on the right chest. The airway is clear and breathing is laboured. What should you do about the wound?
questions.questionZh: 在对一名刺伤病人做快速全身检查（rapid body survey）时，你发现右胸有一个冒泡的开放性伤口。气道通畅，呼吸费力。对这个伤口你应该怎么处理？

options.en: Note its location and seal it during the treatment component after the secondary survey
options.zh: 记下位置，等二级评估之后的处置阶段再封闭

options.en: Pack the wound with hemostatic gauze to stop air entry
options.zh: 用止血纱布填塞伤口，阻止空气进入

options.en: Seal it immediately as a primary survey intervention, then continue the survey
options.zh: 立即封闭伤口——这属于初级评估干预——然后继续检查

options.en: Leave it open so air can escape and prevent a tension pneumothorax
options.zh: 保持伤口开放让空气逸出，以预防张力性气胸

questions.explanationEn: Sealing open chest wounds is listed as a primary survey intervention: life-threatening findings are managed as they are found. Do not pack wounds on the chest. Sealing uses a three-sided occlusive dressing or commercial chest seal, then the survey continues while monitoring for tension pneumothorax.
questions.explanationZh: 封闭胸部开放伤口是初级评估的干预项目之一（第 11 页）：危及生命的问题一经发现就要处理，不能留到处置阶段（A 错）。胸部伤口禁止填塞（第 19 页，B 错）。应使用三边封闭敷料或商用胸封（chest seal）封闭（第 34 页），而不是让伤口敞开（D 错），然后继续检查并密切监测有无张力性气胸。

questions.questionEn: A 35-year-old roofer fell approximately 7 meters onto grass. He is alert, complaining only of left wrist pain, with strong radial pulses and normal breathing. How should he be categorized for transport?
questions.questionZh: 一名 35 岁屋顶工从约 7 米高处坠落到草地上。他神志清楚，只诉左腕疼痛，桡动脉搏动有力，呼吸正常。转运分类应如何判断？

options.en: Stable, because his primary survey shows no life-threatening findings
options.zh: 稳定——初级评估没有发现危及生命的问题

options.en: Unstable, because a free fall of more than 6 metres is a listed mechanism
options.zh: 不稳定——超过 6 米的自由坠落是列明的机制标准

options.en: Stable, because the soft grass absorbed most of the impact
options.zh: 稳定——柔软的草地吸收了大部分冲击

options.en: Unstable only if his vital signs worsen during the secondary survey
options.zh: 只有二级评估中生命体征恶化才算不稳定

questions.explanationEn: BC lists mechanism of injury as an independent route to the unstable category (p.7): a free fall from a height greater than 6 metres (about 20 feet) qualifies on its own. A is wrong because a normal primary survey does not cancel a mechanism criterion. C is wrong because the guideline makes no exception for the landing surface; landing surface is something you record in the fall history (p.12), not a reason to downgrade. D is wrong because waiting for deterioration defeats the purpose of mechanism-based triage - occult internal injury may not show in early vital signs.
questions.explanationZh: BC 把受伤机制列为判定不稳定的独立途径（第 7 页）：从 6 米（约 20 英尺）以上高处自由坠落，单凭这一条就符合。A 错：初级评估正常并不能抵消机制标准。C 错：考纲没有因落地面而降级的例外，落地面是跌倒病史中要记录的内容（第 12 页），不是降级理由。D 错：等生命体征恶化才升级，违背了按机制分诊的初衷——隐匿性内伤早期未必反映在生命体征上。

questions.questionEn: You attend a two-vehicle MVA. Your patient is the restrained driver: GCS 15, normal vital signs, complaining of chest soreness from the seatbelt. The front-seat passenger of the same vehicle was pronounced dead at the scene. How should you categorize him?
questions.questionZh: 你处理一起两车相撞事故。你的病人是系了安全带的驾驶员，GCS 15，生命体征正常，诉安全带勒得胸口酸痛。同车前排乘客已当场死亡。他应如何分类？

options.en: Stable - his own examination and vital signs are all normal
options.zh: 稳定——他本人的检查和生命体征都正常

options.en: Stable - another occupant's death matters only if he was also ejected
options.zh: 稳定——除非他也被甩出车外，否则他人死亡不影响分类

options.en: Unstable only if intrusion on his side of the car exceeded 0.5 m
options.zh: 只有他这一侧车厢侵入超过 0.5 米才算不稳定

options.en: Unstable - a death in the same passenger compartment is a listed criterion
options.zh: 不稳定——同一乘员舱内有人死亡是列明的标准

questions.explanationEn: Death in the passenger compartment is a BC high-risk automobile crash criterion (p.8): forces severe enough to kill one occupant mean survivors are managed as unstable regardless of how they look. A is wrong because mechanism criteria apply even when the examination is normal. B is wrong because ejection is a separate criterion; either one alone is enough. C is wrong on two counts: the intrusion threshold is more than 0.3 m on the occupant side (0.5 m applies to any site, including the roof), and intrusion is an additional criterion, not a precondition.
questions.explanationZh: 同一乘员舱内有人死亡是 BC 高危车祸机制标准之一（第 8 页）：撞击能量大到足以致一人死亡，幸存者无论看起来如何都按不稳定处理。A 错：即使检查结果正常，机制标准照样适用。B 错：被甩出车外是另一条独立标准，任何一条单独成立即可。C 两处都错：乘员侧车厢侵入的门槛是超过 0.3 米（0.5 米指包括车顶在内的任何部位），而且侵入是另一条标准，不是前提条件。

questions.questionEn: A 28-year-old cyclist was struck by a car travelling approximately 40 km/h. She is alert with abrasions and a deformed left forearm, vitals within normal limits. What is the correct transport categorization?
questions.questionZh: 一名 28 岁女性骑自行车时被一辆时速约 40 km/h 的汽车撞倒。她神志清楚，有擦伤，左前臂畸形，生命体征正常。正确的转运分类是什么？

options.en: Unstable - auto versus cyclist at over 30 km/h is a high-risk mechanism
options.zh: 不稳定——汽车撞骑车人且车速超过 30 km/h 属高危机制

options.en: Stable - an isolated forearm fracture is not a proximal long bone injury
options.zh: 稳定——孤立的前臂骨折不属于近端长骨损伤

options.en: Stable - she would be unstable only if she had been thrown over 6 metres
options.zh: 稳定——只有被抛出超过 6 米才算不稳定

options.en: Unstable only if she lost consciousness at any point at the scene
options.zh: 只有她在现场曾经失去意识才算不稳定

questions.explanationEn: Auto versus pedestrian or cyclist at more than 30 km/h is a BC high-risk mechanism (p.8), so she is unstable for transport purposes even though her injuries look limited. B is true about the forearm - it is not a proximal long bone - but the mechanism criterion applies on its own. C is wrong because distance thrown is a history question (p.12), not a BC instability threshold; the 6-metre figure belongs to falls. D is wrong because loss of consciousness is not required when a mechanism criterion is met.
questions.explanationZh: 汽车撞行人或骑车人且车速超过 30 km/h 是 BC 高危机制标准（第 8 页），所以即使她的伤看起来有限，也应按不稳定转运。B 说前臂骨折不属于近端长骨，这一点没错，但机制标准单独成立即可。C 错：被抛出的距离是病史要问的内容（第 12 页），不是 BC 的不稳定门槛，6 米是坠落高度的标准。D 错：符合机制标准时并不要求有意识丧失。

questions.questionEn: In a parking lot, a reversing car bumped a 40-year-old pedestrian at roughly 10-15 km/h. He was knocked down but did not lose consciousness. Primary survey is unremarkable; he has a small scalp abrasion and normal vitals. The best decision is:
questions.questionZh: 停车场里，一辆倒车的汽车以约 10–15 km/h 的速度把一名 40 岁行人撞倒。他没有意识丧失，初级评估无异常，只有头皮小擦伤，生命体征正常。最佳决策是：

options.en: Rapid transport - any auto versus pedestrian collision is a high-risk mechanism
options.zh: 快速转运——任何汽车撞行人都属于高危机制

options.en: Rapid transport - a scalp wound counts as major penetrating head trauma
options.zh: 快速转运——头皮伤口算作头部大穿透伤

options.en: Assess fully on scene - the >30 km/h threshold is not met and he has no unstable findings
options.zh: 在现场完成评估——未达到 30 km/h 的门槛，也没有不稳定表现

options.en: No transport needed - the impact speed was too low to cause injury
options.zh: 不需要转运——撞击速度太低，不会受伤

questions.explanationEn: The BC mechanism criterion is auto versus pedestrian at more than 30 km/h (p.8); a 10-15 km/h parking-lot bump does not meet it, and he has no primary survey or anatomical instability findings (p.7). He is therefore managed as stable: complete the assessment on scene, then transport. A is wrong because the criterion has a speed threshold. B is wrong because a small scalp abrasion is not major penetrating trauma. D is wrong because not meeting the instability criteria does not mean he needs no assessment or transport - he was knocked down and struck his head.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的机制标准是「汽车撞行人且车速超过 30 km/h」（第 8 页）；停车场里 10–15 km/h 的碰撞没有达到，他也没有任何初级评估或解剖学上的不稳定表现（第 7 页）。因此按稳定病人处理：在现场完成评估后再转运。A 错：该标准有车速门槛，并非所有车撞人都算。B 错：头皮小擦伤不属于头部大穿透伤。D 错：不符合不稳定标准不等于不用评估和转运——他被撞倒过，头也碰到了。

questions.questionEn: Which of the following anatomical findings places an adult trauma patient in the unstable category under the BC guidelines?
questions.questionZh: 根据 BC 指南，下列哪一项解剖学发现会将成人创伤病人归入不稳定类别？

options.en: A closed fracture of one wrist with intact distal circulation
options.zh: 单侧腕部闭合骨折，远端循环完好

options.en: Fractures of both femurs
options.zh: 双侧股骨骨折

options.en: A partial thickness burn covering 10% of body surface area on the back
options.zh: 背部 10% 体表面积的部分皮层烧伤

options.en: A single rib fracture with equal air entry
options.zh: 单根肋骨骨折，双侧进气均等

questions.explanationEn: Two or more proximal long bone fractures is a listed anatomical instability criterion; bilateral femur fractures meet it and also carry major hemorrhage risk. A wrist fracture, partial thickness burn of 10% BSA (threshold is >20%), and single rib fracture without instability do not meet the criteria.
questions.explanationZh: 两处及以上近端长骨骨折是解剖学不稳定标准之一；双侧股骨骨折符合，且伴有大出血风险。腕部骨折、10% BSA 的部分皮层烧伤（门槛是 >20%）和无胸壁不稳的单根肋骨骨折都不符合标准。

questions.questionEn: A 45-year-old carpenter amputated his thumb with a table saw. Bleeding is controlled with a pressure dressing, he is calm, and his vital signs are normal. Which statement is correct?
questions.questionZh: 一名 45 岁木工被台锯锯断拇指。加压包扎已控制出血，他情绪平稳，生命体征正常。下列哪项说法正确？

options.en: Unstable - any traumatic amputation is an anatomical instability criterion
options.zh: 不稳定——任何创伤性截肢都属于解剖学不稳定标准

options.en: Place the thumb directly on ice to keep the tissue as cold as possible
options.zh: 把断指直接放在冰上，让组织尽量保持低温

options.en: Apply a tourniquet even though direct pressure has controlled the bleeding
options.zh: 即使直接压迫已止血，也要上止血带

options.en: Stable - only amputations proximal to the wrist or ankle meet the criterion
options.zh: 稳定——只有腕或踝以近的截肢才符合该标准

questions.explanationEn: BC's anatomical criterion is amputation proximal to the wrist or ankle (p.7); a thumb amputation with controlled bleeding does not meet it, so he is managed as stable. A is wrong because the criterion is level-specific, not 'any amputation'. B is wrong because the amputated-parts procedure (p.20) says never place the part directly on ice: rinse it with cool sterile water, wrap it loosely in saline-moistened sterile gauze, bag it, keep it cool in a protective container, and transport it with the patient. C is wrong because a tourniquet is used only when direct pressure fails to control bleeding (p.19).
questions.explanationZh: BC 的解剖学标准是「腕或踝以近的截肢」（第 7 页）；出血已控制的拇指离断不符合，所以按稳定病人处理。A 错：该标准限定了截肢平面，并非任何截肢都算。B 错：断肢保存流程（第 20 页）明确禁止把断肢直接放在冰上，应先用凉的无菌水冲洗，用生理盐水浸湿的无菌纱布松松包好，装进塑料袋，放入保护容器保持低温，随病人一起转运。C 错：止血带只在直接压迫无法止血时才使用（第 19 页）。

questions.questionEn: A welder has a full thickness burn that completely encircles his right forearm, estimated at 5% BSA. He is alert with normal vitals and severe pain. How is he categorized?
questions.questionZh: 一名焊工右前臂全层烧伤，烧伤环绕前臂一整圈，估计面积 5%。他神志清楚，生命体征正常，疼痛剧烈。他应如何分类？

options.en: Unstable - a circumferential limb burn qualifies regardless of BSA
options.zh: 不稳定——环绕肢体一圈的烧伤不论面积都符合标准

options.en: Stable - full thickness burns count only when they exceed 10% BSA
options.zh: 稳定——全层烧伤超过 10% 体表面积才算

options.en: Stable - the burn does not involve the face, hands, or airway
options.zh: 稳定——烧伤没有累及面部、手或气道

options.en: Unstable only if his distal pulses have already been lost
options.zh: 只有远端脉搏已经消失才算不稳定

questions.explanationEn: BC's major burns list (p.7) includes burns that fully encircle a limb as a separate item, independent of the BSA thresholds, because a circumferential burn can act like a tourniquet as swelling develops. B is wrong because the >10% full-thickness threshold is only one of several burn criteria; meeting any one is enough. C is wrong because the face, hands, and airway are separate criteria, not the only special areas. D is wrong because waiting for pulses to disappear means waiting for the limb-threatening complication to happen.
questions.explanationZh: BC 重度烧伤清单（第 7 页）把「环绕肢体一整圈的烧伤」单列为一条，与烧伤面积门槛无关，因为环形烧伤随着肿胀加重会像止血带一样勒住肢体。B 错：全层烧伤 > 10% 只是几条烧伤标准之一，符合任何一条即可。C 错：面部、手和气道是另外几条标准，并不是唯一的特殊部位。D 错：等远端脉搏消失才升级，等于坐等危及肢体的并发症发生。

questions.questionEn: Which primary survey finding places an adult patient in the unstable category for examination purposes?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪个 primary survey 发现会使成人病人被归为不稳定（考试标准）？

options.en: Heart rate of 96 with warm, dry skin
options.zh: 心率 96，皮肤温暖干燥

options.en: Localized abdominal tenderness with normal vitals
options.zh: 局限性腹部压痛，vitals 正常

options.en: Absent radial pulses
options.zh: 桡动脉搏动消失

options.en: Pain rated 8 out of 10 from an isolated ankle injury
options.zh: 孤立踝部损伤，疼痛评分 8/10

questions.explanationEn: Absent radial pulses appear on the primary survey instability list - they suggest significant hypotension or peripheral shutdown from shock. Tachycardia alone with good skin, localized tenderness, or severe pain from a minor injury do not by themselves meet the listed criteria.
questions.explanationZh: 桡动脉搏动消失在 primary survey 不稳定清单中——提示明显低血压或休克导致的外周灌注关闭。单纯轻度心率增快伴皮肤良好、局限性压痛、或小伤口的剧烈疼痛本身都不在清单标准内。

questions.questionEn: A 40-year-old fell from a ladder. He opens his eyes when you speak to him, is confused about where he is and the date, and follows your command to squeeze your fingers. What is his GCS and injury classification?
questions.questionZh: 一名 40 岁男性从梯子上摔下。你和他说话时他会睁眼，对地点和日期表述混乱（confused），但能按指令握你的手指。他的 GCS 是多少？属于哪一级损伤？

options.en: GCS 11 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 11 —— 中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 13 - mild traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 13 —— 轻度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 15 - no brain injury
options.zh: GCS 15 —— 无脑损伤

options.en: GCS 9 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 9 —— 中度创伤性脑损伤

questions.explanationEn: Eye opening to voice scores 3, confused speech scores 4, obeying commands scores 6: total GCS 13. Per the guideline, a GCS of 13 or higher indicates mild traumatic brain injury. Note that confused but converses is V4, not V3 (inappropriate words).
questions.explanationZh: 呼唤睁眼 E3，言语混乱 V4，遵嘱动作 M6，合计 GCS 13。按指南，GCS ≥ 13 提示轻度创伤性脑损伤。注意「混乱但能对话」是 V4，而不是 V3（不恰当言语）。

questions.questionEn: An assault victim opens his eyes only to a trapezius squeeze, makes incomprehensible moaning sounds, and withdraws his arm from the painful stimulus. What is his GCS and classification?
questions.questionZh: 一名被殴打的伤者只有在斜方肌掐捏时才睁眼，发出无法理解的呻吟声，并会从疼痛刺激中回缩手臂。他的 GCS 和分级是什么？

options.en: GCS 10 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 10 —— 中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 6 - severe traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 6 —— 重度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 9 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 9 —— 中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 8 - severe traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 8 —— 重度创伤性脑损伤

questions.explanationEn: Eye opening to pain scores 2, incomprehensible sounds score 2, withdrawal from pain scores 4: total GCS 8. A GCS of 8 or less is defined as severe traumatic brain injury, with implications for aggressive airway monitoring and rapid transport.
questions.explanationZh: 疼痛刺激睁眼 E2，无法理解的声音 V2，疼痛回缩 M4，合计 GCS 8。GCS ≤ 8 定义为重度创伤性脑损伤，意味着需要严密的气道管理和快速转运。

questions.questionEn: Following a motorcycle crash, a rider has no eye opening to any stimulus, makes no sounds, and extends both arms rigidly when a painful stimulus is applied. What is his GCS?
questions.questionZh: 摩托车事故后，一名骑手对任何刺激均不睁眼、不发声，疼痛刺激时双臂僵硬伸直（extension）。他的 GCS 是多少？

options.en: GCS 4
options.zh: GCS 4

options.en: GCS 3
options.zh: GCS 3

options.en: GCS 6
options.zh: GCS 6

options.en: GCS 5
options.zh: GCS 5

questions.explanationEn: No eye opening scores 1, no verbal response scores 1, and extension to pain scores 2, totalling GCS 4 - a severe traumatic brain injury. Extension (decerebrate) scores 2 while abnormal flexion (decorticate) scores 3; confusing the two is a common exam error. The minimum possible GCS is 3, not 0.
questions.explanationZh: 不睁眼 E1，无言语 V1，疼痛刺激伸直（去大脑强直）M2，合计 GCS 4，属重度创伤性脑损伤。伸直（decerebrate）计 2 分，异常屈曲（decorticate）计 3 分，两者混淆是常见考试错误。GCS 最低分是 3 而不是 0。

questions.questionEn: A 33-year-old with a lacerated thigh has these serial vitals - on arrival: HR 92, BP 128/84, RR 18, skin warm; 15 minutes later: HR 118, BP 96/72, RR 24, skin cool and pale. What do these trends indicate?
questions.questionZh: 一名 33 岁大腿裂伤病人的连续生命体征如下——到达时：HR 92，BP 128/84，RR 18，皮肤温暖；15 分钟后：HR 118，BP 96/72，RR 24，皮肤发凉、苍白。这一趋势提示什么？

options.en: Anxiety response - the falling BP shows the patient is calming down
options.zh: 焦虑反应——血压下降说明病人正在平静下来

options.en: Progressing hemorrhagic shock - he is now unstable and needs rapid transport
options.zh: 失血性休克在进展——他已属不稳定，需要快速转运

options.en: Normal variation - both sets of readings fall within adult reference ranges
options.zh: 正常波动——两组读数都在成人参考范围内

options.en: Improving perfusion - the rising heart rate shows effective compensation
options.zh: 灌注在改善——心率上升说明代偿有效

questions.explanationEn: Rising heart rate and respiratory rate with a falling blood pressure and skin turning cool and pale is the trajectory of hemorrhagic shock progressing toward decompensation. Cool pale clammy skin secondary to suspected shock is itself a BC primary survey instability criterion (p.7), and the hypovolemia protocol applies (p.54): control the bleeding, position supine, keep warm, give oxygen, and transport. A is wrong because anxiety raises blood pressure rather than dropping it 30 mmHg with cooling skin. C is wrong because judging each reading in isolation misses the trend. D is wrong because tachycardia with a falling pressure means compensation is failing, not succeeding.
questions.explanationZh: 心率、呼吸频率上升，血压下降，皮肤转为发凉苍白，这是失血性休克向失代偿发展的轨迹。「疑似休克所致的湿冷苍白皮肤」本身就是 BC 初级评估的不稳定标准（第 7 页），应按低血容量（Hypovolemia）协议处理（第 54 页）：止血、平卧、保暖、给氧并转运。A 错：焦虑会使血压升高，而不是让血压掉 30 mmHg 并伴皮肤变凉。C 错：把每组读数单独对照正常值，会漏掉恶化趋势。D 错：心率加快而血压下降，说明代偿正在失败，而不是代偿有效。

questions.questionEn: A 26-year-old struck his head snowboarding. During transport his BP climbs from 130/76 to 172/60, his heart rate falls from 88 to 54, and his respirations become irregular. His right pupil is now sluggish. This pattern most likely represents:
questions.questionZh: 一名 26 岁男子玩滑雪板时摔倒撞到头部。转运途中，他的血压从 130/76 升到 172/60，心率从 88 降到 54，呼吸变得不规则，右侧瞳孔对光反应迟钝。这一表现最可能代表：

options.en: Hypovolemic shock from an associated internal bleed
options.zh: 合并内出血引起的低血容量性休克

options.en: A vagal response triggered by pain and anxiety
options.zh: 疼痛和焦虑诱发的迷走反应

options.en: Early anaphylaxis from an unrecognized allergen exposure
options.zh: 未察觉的过敏原暴露引起的早期过敏性休克

options.en: Rising intracranial pressure from an expanding brain injury
options.zh: 脑损伤扩大导致颅内压升高

questions.explanationEn: Rising systolic pressure with a widening pulse pressure, a falling heart rate, irregular respirations, and a newly sluggish pupil are the classic signs of rising intracranial pressure (the Cushing response) after head trauma. A is wrong because hypovolemic shock produces the opposite pattern - falling BP and rising HR. B is wrong because a vagal response lowers both heart rate and blood pressure and does not change the pupils. C is wrong because anaphylaxis causes hypotension and tachycardia, often with urticaria or wheeze. Management follows the BC TBI guideline (p.27): SpO2 of 94% or higher, assist ventilation if needed, head of bed at 30 degrees, loosen the collar, and notify the receiving facility.
questions.explanationZh: 头部外伤后出现收缩压升高、脉压增宽、心率下降、呼吸不规则，再加上新出现的单侧瞳孔反应迟钝，这是颅内压升高的典型表现（库欣反应，Cushing response）。A 错：低血容量性休克正好相反——血压下降、心率加快。B 错：迷走反应会使心率和血压同时下降，也不会引起瞳孔变化。C 错：过敏性休克（anaphylaxis）表现为低血压和心动过速，常伴荨麻疹或哮鸣音。处理按 BC 创伤性脑损伤（TBI）指南（第 27 页）：维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%，必要时辅助通气，床头抬高 30 度，松开硬质颈托，并通知接收医院。

questions.questionEn: A physician orders 1000 mL of normal saline over 6 hours during a long transfer. Your set delivers 10 gtts/mL. What drip rate do you run?
questions.questionZh: 长途转运中，医嘱要求在 6 小时内输入 1000 mL 生理盐水，你的输液器为 10 gtts/mL。滴速应是多少？

options.en: 17 gtts/min
options.zh: 17 gtts/min

options.en: 28 gtts/min
options.zh: 28 gtts/min

options.en: 42 gtts/min
options.zh: 42 gtts/min

options.en: 167 gtts/min
options.zh: 167 gtts/min

questions.explanationEn: 1000 mL x 10 gtts/mL / 360 minutes = 10000 / 360 = approximately 28 gtts/min (formula on p.39). 167 gtts/min is the micro-drip error (using 60 gtts/mL); 17 gtts/min comes from using 10 hours instead of 6; 42 gtts/min comes from using 4 hours.
questions.explanationZh: 1000 mL × 10 gtts/mL ÷ 360 分钟 = 10000 ÷ 360 ≈ 28 gtts/min（公式见第 39 页）。167 是误用了微滴管 60 gtts/mL 的系数；17 是把时间错算成 10 小时；42 是把时间错算成 4 小时。

questions.questionEn: When a BC protocol refers to running an IV at a maintenance rate, what flow rate does this correspond to?
questions.questionZh: BC 协议中提到的「维持速度（maintenance rate）」大约相当于多大的输液流速？

options.en: Approximately 75 mL/hr
options.zh: 约 75 mL/hr

options.en: Approximately 150 mL/hr
options.zh: 约 150 mL/hr

options.en: Approximately 30 mL/hr
options.zh: 约 30 mL/hr

options.en: A wide-open line until 500 mL has infused
options.zh: 全速输注，直到输完 500 mL

questions.explanationEn: The IV maintenance section states that the maintenance rate is approximately 75 mL/hr, delivered through either a 10 gtts/mL macro-drip or a 60 gtts/mL micro-drip set. 150 mL/hr and 30 mL/hr are not the guideline figure. A wide-open line is how a fluid bolus is run; a bolus is volume-targeted (20 mL/kg) to correct hypoperfusion and is a different order from a maintenance rate.
questions.explanationZh: 静脉输液维持（IV Maintenance）一节写明，维持速度约为 75 mL/hr，可用 10 gtts/mL 的大滴管或 60 gtts/mL 的微滴管输注。150 mL/hr 和 30 mL/hr 都不是考纲给出的数值。全速输注是液体冲击的做法，冲击量按 20 mL/kg 计算、用于纠正低灌注，与维持速度是两回事。

questions.questionEn: During transport with a running IV, how often does the BC IV maintenance guideline direct you to reassess the patient and the IV, and what does the check include?
questions.questionZh: 转运途中有静脉输液在进行时，BC 静脉输液维持指南要求多久重评一次病人和输液？评估包括什么？

options.en: Every 30 minutes - vital signs and the volume left in the bag
options.zh: 每 30 分钟——生命体征和液袋剩余量

options.en: Every 15-30 minutes - the drip rate, site, and tubing only
options.zh: 每 15–30 分钟——只查滴速、穿刺点和管路

options.en: Every 5-15 minutes - ABCs, vital signs, the site, tubing, and bag
options.zh: 每 5–15 分钟——ABC、生命体征、穿刺点、管路和液袋

options.en: On arrival at hospital - when the total volume infused is recorded
options.zh: 到达医院时——记录总输入量时再查

questions.explanationEn: The BC IV maintenance section (p.39) directs regular reassessment every 5-15 minutes: ABCs and injury sites, vital signs, inspection of the IV site, tubing and solution bag, observation for complications, maintenance of the flow rate, and changing the bag when required. A and B use intervals that are too long, and B leaves out the patient-side checks (ABCs, vital signs). D is wrong because complications such as infiltration or fluid overload must be caught during transport, not after it.
questions.explanationZh: BC 静脉输液维持（IV Maintenance）一节（第 39 页）要求每 5–15 分钟定期重评：ABC 与受伤部位、生命体征，检查穿刺点、管路和液袋，观察并发症，维持正确滴速，必要时更换液袋。A 和 B 的间隔都太长，B 还漏掉了病人本身的评估（ABC、生命体征）。D 错：渗漏、液体过负荷等并发症必须在转运途中发现，不能等到医院才查。

questions.questionEn: A transfer document states the patient has been 'NPO since 0600, salbutamol prn'. Using the BC abbreviation list, this means the patient:
questions.questionZh: 转院文件上写着病人「NPO since 0600, salbutamol prn」。按 BC 缩写表，这表示病人：

options.en: Has had nothing by mouth since 0600 and takes salbutamol as needed
options.zh: 自 06:00 起禁食禁水，沙丁胺醇（salbutamol）按需使用

options.en: Has had no pain since 0600 and takes salbutamol nightly
options.zh: 自 06:00 起无疼痛，沙丁胺醇每晚使用

options.en: Received nitrous oxide at 0600 and salbutamol before meals
options.zh: 06:00 吸过笑气（nitrous oxide），沙丁胺醇餐前使用

options.en: Was non-palpable for pulses at 0600 and needs salbutamol immediately
options.zh: 06:00 时摸不到脉搏，需要立即给沙丁胺醇

questions.explanationEn: On the BC abbreviation list, NPO means nothing by mouth and prn means as needed or as required. B confuses prn with hs (at bedtime). C confuses NPO with nitrous oxide and prn with ac (before meals). D confuses prn with stat (immediately). Misreading standard abbreviations on transfer paperwork is a real medication-safety hazard.
questions.explanationZh: 按 BC 缩写表，NPO 意为禁食禁水（nothing by mouth），prn 意为按需使用（as needed）。B 把 prn 当成了 hs（睡前）。C 把 NPO 当成了笑气（nitrous oxide），又把 prn 当成了 ac（餐前）。D 把 prn 当成了 stat（立即）。误读转院文书上的标准缩写会带来真实的用药安全风险。

questions.questionEn: After a call involving an intoxicated patient who initially refused care, which entry is the most appropriate way to document his behaviour on the Patient Care Report?
questions.questionZh: 处理一名起初拒绝救治的醉酒病人后，下列哪一条病人救护记录（Patient Care Report, PCR）写法最恰当？

options.en: Pt intoxicated and uncooperative; refused care, later agreed to go
options.zh: 「病人醉酒、不合作；起初拒绝救治，后来同意去医院」

options.en: Pt appeared drunk; refusal not recorded since he ended up consenting
options.zh: 「病人看起来醉了；因最终同意，拒绝过程不予记录」

options.en: AOB, slurred speech; pt said 'I don't need help'; risks explained; consented 2145
options.zh: 「呼气有酒味，言语含糊；病人说『我不需要帮助』；已说明风险；21:45 同意」

options.en: Known ETOH abuser from previous calls to this address; difficult as usual
options.zh: 「以往多次出车已知为酗酒者；和往常一样难缠」

questions.explanationEn: Good documentation records objective findings, the patient's own words, what you did, and times. C does all four: AOB (alcohol on breath) and slurred speech are observations, the refusal is quoted, the risk discussion is noted, and the time of consent is recorded. A is wrong because 'intoxicated' and 'uncooperative' are conclusions without the observations behind them. B is wrong because an initial refusal is a legally significant event that must be documented even if the patient later consents. D is wrong because labels and references to past calls are judgmental and are not findings from this encounter.
questions.explanationZh: 好的记录应写客观发现、病人原话、你做了什么以及时间。C 四项齐全：呼气有酒味（AOB）和言语含糊是观察所见，拒绝用病人原话记录，注明已说明风险，并写下同意的时间。A 错：「醉酒」「不合作」是结论，没有写出支撑结论的观察。B 错：最初的拒绝在法律上很重要，即使病人后来同意也必须记录。D 错：贴标签、提以往出车经历属于主观评价，不是本次接触的发现。

questions.questionEn: A 78-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes calls for 'indigestion' that started 2 hours ago. She is weak, diaphoretic, and slightly short of breath, but denies any chest pain. Her vitals: HR 96, BP 142/88, SpO2 93%. The most appropriate approach is to:
questions.questionZh: 一名患 2 型糖尿病的 78 岁女性因 2 小时前开始的「消化不良」呼叫救护。她乏力、出汗、轻度气促，但否认任何胸痛。生命体征：HR 96，BP 142/88，SpO2 93%。最恰当的处理是：

options.en: Treat it as indigestion and advise follow-up with her family doctor
options.zh: 按消化不良处理，建议她之后看家庭医生

options.en: Manage as possible cardiac ischemia per the cardiac chest pain guideline
options.zh: 按可能的心肌缺血处理，依心源性胸痛指南处置

options.en: Give oral glucose first, since diabetics often present this way when low
options.zh: 先给口服葡萄糖（oral glucose），糖尿病人低血糖时常这样表现

options.en: Have her walk to the stretcher so you can judge her exercise tolerance
options.zh: 让她走到担架旁，借此判断她的活动耐量

questions.explanationEn: Older adults, women, and people with diabetes often present with ischemia as epigastric discomfort, weakness, diaphoresis, or dyspnea without chest pain. BC's ASA monograph (p.60) lists atypical symptoms consistent with cardiac ischemia as an indication, and the cardiac chest pain guideline (p.47) applies: position of comfort, oxygen to SpO2 of 94% or higher, ASA, and transport. A is wrong because labelling this indigestion misses a likely MI. C is wrong because glucose is given only after a blood glucose check confirms hypoglycemia; sweating and breathlessness do not prove a low sugar. D is wrong because walking increases myocardial oxygen demand - the guideline says to limit movement.
questions.explanationZh: 老年人、女性和糖尿病患者发生心肌缺血时，常表现为上腹不适、乏力、出汗或气促，而没有胸痛。BC 阿司匹林（ASA）药物专论（第 60 页）把「符合心肌缺血的不典型症状」列为指征，应按心源性胸痛（Cardiac Chest Pain）指南处理（第 47 页）：舒适体位、给氧维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%、给予阿司匹林（ASA）并转运。A 错：当成消化不良会漏掉很可能的心肌梗死。C 错：只有测血糖确认低血糖后才给葡萄糖（glucose），出汗和气促并不能证明血糖低。D 错：行走会增加心肌耗氧，指南要求限制病人活动。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.47, p.60; Nancy Ch 45

questions.questionEn: An 82-year-old man on metoprolol has had black, tarry stools for two days. He is pale and diaphoretic with cool skin. His heart rate is 84 and his BP is 104/70. How should you interpret his heart rate?
questions.questionZh: 一名服用美托洛尔（metoprolol）的 82 岁男性已解黑色柏油样便两天。他面色苍白、出汗、皮肤发凉，心率 84，血压 104/70。你应如何解读这个心率？

options.en: A rate of 84 shows that his blood loss is minor and well compensated
options.zh: 心率 84 说明他失血不多、代偿良好

options.en: Skin signs are unreliable in the elderly, so the heart rate is the better guide
options.zh: 老年人皮肤征象不可靠，心率才是更好的指标

options.en: With a systolic above 90, a rate of 84 effectively rules out hemorrhagic shock
options.zh: 收缩压高于 90，加上心率 84，基本可排除失血性休克

options.en: His beta blocker can blunt the tachycardia of blood loss, so 84 may hide shock
options.zh: β 受体阻滞剂会压住失血时的心率加快，84 可能掩盖了休克

questions.explanationEn: Beta blockers prevent the compensatory rise in heart rate that normally signals blood loss, so older patients on these drugs may be in significant shock with a 'normal' rate. His skin signs - pale, cool, diaphoretic - are the more reliable indicator here and meet BC's instability criterion of cool pale clammy skin secondary to suspected shock (p.7). A is wrong because the rate is pharmacologically capped and cannot show how much blood he has lost. B reverses the truth: in a beta-blocked patient, skin signs are more trustworthy than the pulse. C is wrong because the hypovolemia protocol can be used above 90 mmHg when shock is anticipated (p.54), and an older patient's 'normal' BP may already be a large drop from baseline.
questions.explanationZh: β 受体阻滞剂会抑制失血时本该出现的代偿性心率加快，因此服用这类药的老年人可能已处于明显休克，心率却显示「正常」。这时他的皮肤征象——苍白、发凉、出汗——更可靠，已符合 BC「疑似休克所致湿冷苍白皮肤」的不稳定标准（第 7 页）。A 错：心率被药物压住了，反映不出失血多少。B 正好说反了：对服用 β 阻滞剂的病人，皮肤征象比脉搏更可信。C 错：预计会发生休克时，收缩压高于 90 也可启用低血容量协议（第 54 页），而且老年人的「正常」血压可能已比基线下降很多。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.7, p.54; Nancy Ch 27

questions.questionEn: A 79-year-old woman on warfarin tripped on a rug, struck her head on the floor, and got up by herself. She has a small forehead bruise, GCS 15, and no complaints. Her son asks if she really needs to go to hospital. Your best response is based on which reasoning?
questions.questionZh: 一名服用华法林（warfarin）的 79 岁女性被地毯绊倒，头撞到地板，自己站了起来。她前额有一小块瘀青，GCS 15，没有不适。她儿子问她是否真有必要去医院。你的最佳回答应基于哪种判断？

options.en: She can stay home, since her GCS is 15 and the fall was from standing height
options.zh: 可以留在家里——GCS 15，而且只是站立高度跌倒

options.en: She can stay home if her son watches her and calls if she starts to vomit
options.zh: 可以留在家里，只要儿子看着她、出现呕吐再打电话

options.en: Warfarin raises her risk of a delayed brain bleed, so she needs hospital assessment
options.zh: 华法林增加了迟发性颅内出血的风险，所以需要到医院评估

options.en: Warfarin prevents clots, so her risk of a bleed in the head is actually lower
options.zh: 华法林能防止血栓，所以她颅内出血的风险反而更低

questions.explanationEn: Patients on anticoagulants are at increased risk of severe bleeding, and even minor head injuries in initially asymptomatic patients can lead to catastrophic results, so they need timely hospital assessment. Age-related brain atrophy also leaves room for a bleed to expand before signs appear. A is wrong because a normal GCS at first contact does not exclude a slowly expanding bleed. B is wrong because home observation delays diagnosis until she deteriorates. D is wrong because preventing clot formation is exactly what makes bleeding harder to stop.
questions.explanationZh: 服用抗凝药的病人出血风险更高，即使最初没有症状，轻微头部外伤也可能导致灾难性后果，因此需要及时到医院评估。老年人脑萎缩也让出血在出现症状之前有更多扩大的空间。A 错：首次接触时 GCS 正常，不能排除缓慢扩大的出血。B 错：在家观察会把诊断拖到她病情恶化时。D 错：华法林（warfarin）抑制凝血，恰恰让出血更难止住。

questions.questionEn: An 81-year-old man fell in his kitchen. He has a painful hip and abrasions. While gathering the fall history, which question is most important for uncovering a treatable medical cause?
questions.questionZh: 一名 81 岁男性在厨房跌倒，髋部疼痛并有擦伤。采集跌倒病史时，哪个问题最有助于发现可治疗的内科病因？

options.en: Did you hit your head or black out at all when you landed?
options.zh: 「落地时你撞到头或昏过去了吗？」

options.en: Did you feel dizzy, faint, or have palpitations just before you fell?
options.zh: 「摔倒前一刻你有没有头晕、要晕倒的感觉或心慌？」

options.en: Have you fallen in the house before, and how often does it happen?
options.zh: 「你以前在家里摔过吗？多久摔一次？」

options.en: How long were you lying on the floor before anyone found you?
options.zh: 「你在地上躺了多久才被人发现？」

questions.explanationEn: BC's fall history list includes the cause of the fall (p.12), and in older adults a fall is often the first sign of a medical event - syncope, dysrhythmia, hypoglycemia, stroke, or a medication effect. Asking about symptoms just before the fall separates a mechanical trip from a medical cause. A matters for injury assessment (head injury, loss of consciousness) but does not identify why he fell. C is useful for fall-risk follow-up but does not reveal today's trigger. D matters for the complications of a long lie, such as hypothermia and pressure injury, rather than the cause.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的跌倒病史清单包括「跌倒原因」（第 12 页）。老年人跌倒常常是内科事件的首发表现——晕厥、心律失常、低血糖、卒中或药物作用。问清跌倒前一刻的症状，才能区分单纯绊倒和内科原因。A 对评估损伤（头部外伤、意识丧失）很重要，但回答不了他为什么会摔倒。C 有助于以后评估跌倒风险，却找不出这次的诱因。D 关系到长时间倒地的并发症（低体温、压伤），而不是跌倒原因。

questions.questionEn: Care aides report that an 86-year-old woman with dementia 'seems confused'. She is calm, answers some questions oddly, and vitals are normal. What is the single most useful piece of information to obtain next?
questions.questionZh: 护理人员说一名 86 岁的失智女性「看起来糊涂了」。她情绪平静，有些问题答得古怪，生命体征正常。接下来最有价值的一项信息是什么？

options.en: A Mini-Mental State Examination score to quantify her confusion
options.zh: 做一次简易精神状态检查（MMSE），把混乱程度量化

options.en: Whether she has an advance directive or DNR order on file
options.zh: 她是否有预立医疗指示或不复苏（DNR）医嘱

options.en: Her baseline mental status from staff - is today different from her usual?
options.zh: 向护理人员了解她的基线精神状态——今天和平时有没有不同

options.en: Her temperature, since only a fever would point to an acute cause
options.zh: 量体温，因为只有发热才提示急性病因

questions.explanationEn: In a patient with dementia, confusion cannot be interpreted without knowing her baseline. An acute change from her usual state suggests delirium, which in older adults signals physical illness or a drug effect (infection, hypoglycemia, hypoxia, stroke, medication) and needs a full assessment including blood glucose. A is wrong because a one-time score without a baseline cannot show whether anything has changed. B is relevant to goals of care but does not help interpret her presentation. D is wrong because older adults with serious infection often have little or no fever, so temperature cannot be the deciding test.
questions.explanationZh: 对失智病人来说，不知道基线就无法解读「糊涂」。与平时相比的急性变化提示谵妄（delirium），而老年人的谵妄是躯体疾病或药物作用的信号（感染、低血糖、缺氧、卒中、药物），需要包括血糖在内的全面评估。A 错：没有基线的一次性评分看不出有没有变化。B 关系到照护目标，但无助于解读她现在的表现。D 错：老年人严重感染时常常只有轻微发热甚至不发热，体温不能作为决定性依据。

questions.questionEn: An 85-year-old woman with a history of recurrent UTIs has become withdrawn and confused over 24 hours. Temperature 36.4, HR 92, BP 108/64, RR 20. Her daughter says 'at least she has no fever, so it can't be an infection.' Your assessment should recognize that:
questions.questionZh: 一名有反复尿路感染史的 85 岁女性在 24 小时内变得淡漠、意识混乱。体温 36.4°C，HR 92，BP 108/64，RR 20。她女儿说：「至少没发烧，应该不是感染。」你的评估应认识到：

options.en: A normal temperature makes infection unlikely, so look for a neurological cause
options.zh: 体温正常说明感染可能性不大，应寻找神经系统原因

options.en: Older adults often mount little or no fever; new confusion may be the main sign of infection
options.zh: 老年人感染时常常低热或不发热，新发意识混乱可能就是感染的主要表现

options.en: Confusion developing over a day is most likely progression of underlying dementia
options.zh: 一天内出现的意识混乱，最可能是原有失智加重

options.en: Sepsis would cause hypothermia, so a temperature of 36.4 argues against it
options.zh: 脓毒症会引起低体温，36.4°C 反而不支持脓毒症

questions.explanationEn: Nancy notes that in older adults fever may be minimal or absent with serious infection, and many acute illnesses present simply as delirium. New withdrawal and confusion over 24 hours in a woman with recurrent UTIs and borderline vital signs should be treated as possible sepsis. A is wrong because a normal temperature does not make infection unlikely at her age. C is wrong because dementia progresses over months; a change over 24 hours is delirium until proven otherwise. D is wrong because sepsis does not reliably cause hypothermia, and a normal temperature does not exclude it. Assess fully, including blood glucose, and transport.
questions.explanationZh: 教材（Nancy）指出，老年人发生严重感染时可能只有轻微发热甚至不发热，许多急性疾病只表现为谵妄。一名反复尿路感染的女性 24 小时内变得淡漠、糊涂，生命体征处于临界，应按可能的脓毒症处理。A 错：在她这个年龄，体温正常并不能说明感染可能性小。C 错：失智是以月为单位进展的，24 小时内出现的变化在排除之前都应视为谵妄。D 错：脓毒症并不一定引起低体温，体温正常也不能排除它。应全面评估（包括血糖）并转运。

questions.questionEn: Assessing an 88-year-old man for 'a fall', you find bruises on his forearms and back in several different stages of healing. His story of the fall keeps changing, and his adult son answers most questions for him while standing close. What is your most appropriate course of action?
questions.questionZh: 你因「跌倒」去评估一名 88 岁男性，发现他前臂和背部有多处处于不同愈合阶段的瘀伤。他对跌倒经过的说法前后不一，他的成年儿子紧站在旁边，大多数问题都替他回答。你最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Talk to him alone if possible, document objectively, transport, and report it
options.zh: 尽量单独和他谈，客观记录，转运，并上报疑虑

options.en: Accept the family's account and document 'multiple falls' as the cause
options.zh: 接受家属的说法，在记录中写「多次跌倒」作为原因

options.en: Remain on scene and wait for police before making any transport decision
options.zh: 留在现场，等警察来了再决定是否转运

options.en: Confront the son at the scene and ask him to explain the bruises
options.zh: 当场质问儿子，要求他解释这些瘀伤

questions.explanationEn: Injuries in different stages of healing that do not fit the story, a changing account, and a caregiver who answers for the patient are recognized clues to elder maltreatment. Nancy's guidance is to listen to the patient, document your observations carefully, transport if he will accept it, and report your findings and suspicions to the receiving facility, notifying law enforcement if the situation is immediately unsafe. B is wrong because recording a cause you doubt hides the findings and fails your duty to report. C is wrong because police are needed only if the scene is unsafe; waiting delays care for a patient who needs assessment and removal from the situation. D is wrong because confronting the suspected abuser can escalate the danger to the patient and the crew.
questions.explanationZh: 伤痕处于不同愈合阶段且与描述不符、经过说法前后不一、照护者抢着替病人回答，这些都是公认的老人虐待（elder maltreatment）线索。教材（Nancy）的建议是：耐心听病人讲，仔细记录观察所见，病人同意的话就转运，并把发现和疑虑报告给接收医院；现场若有即时危险则报警。B 错：把自己怀疑的原因照抄进记录，等于掩盖发现，也没有履行报告责任。C 错：只有现场不安全时才需要等警察，干等会耽误一位需要评估、也需要离开这个环境的病人。D 错：当面质问疑似施虐者可能让病人和救护人员更危险。

questions.questionEn: An 88-year-old woman with known osteoporosis slipped from a low step and landed on her buttocks. She has midline mid-back pain but can move all limbs, with normal vitals. Which reasoning should guide your management?
questions.questionZh: 一名已知骨质疏松的 88 岁女性从矮台阶上滑下，臀部着地。她诉背部正中段疼痛，四肢活动正常，生命体征正常。哪种判断应指导你的处置？

options.en: A fall from a low step lacks the energy to fracture the spine; no precautions needed
options.zh: 矮台阶跌倒能量不足以造成脊柱骨折，不需要保护

options.en: Moving all four limbs normally excludes a significant spinal fracture
options.zh: 四肢活动正常，可以排除严重脊柱骨折

options.en: Give analgesia and leave her home on bed rest, as these fractures are stable
options.zh: 给镇痛后让她在家卧床，这类骨折都是稳定的

options.en: Osteoporotic bone breaks with little force; assess and protect her spine
options.zh: 骨质疏松的骨头受很小外力就会断，应评估并保护脊柱

questions.explanationEn: Osteoporosis in the thoracic and lumbar spine contributes to a high rate of fractures in older patients, and vertebral compression fractures can follow trivial falls. Midline back pain after any fall in an 88-year-old with osteoporosis warrants spinal assessment, spinal motion restriction as indicated (p.25), and transport. A is wrong because osteoporosis breaks the usual link between mechanism and injury. B is wrong because normal limb movement does not exclude a vertebral fracture, including an unstable one. C is wrong because the fracture type cannot be determined in the field and she needs imaging; leaving her at home with a suspected fracture is unsafe.
questions.explanationZh: 胸腰椎骨质疏松使老年人骨折率很高，椎体压缩性骨折可以发生在很轻微的跌倒之后。88 岁、已知骨质疏松的病人跌倒后出现背部正中疼痛，应进行脊柱评估，按指征实施脊柱活动限制（第 25 页）并转运。A 错：骨质疏松打破了「机制轻就伤不重」的常规对应。B 错：四肢活动正常不能排除椎体骨折，包括不稳定骨折。C 错：现场无法判断骨折类型，她需要影像检查，怀疑骨折却把她留在家里是不安全的。

questions.questionEn: An 80-year-old woman fell against a coffee table. She is alert with a bleeding laceration above her right eyebrow and neck stiffness. Which primary survey intervention indication applies?
questions.questionZh: 一名 80 岁女性跌倒撞到茶几。她神志清楚，右眉上方有一处正在出血的裂伤，并感到颈部僵硬。适用哪一条初级评估干预指征？

options.en: Airway procedures - a facial laceration predicts airway compromise
options.zh: 气道处理——面部裂伤预示气道将受影响

options.en: Cervical spine stabilization - she has an obvious injury above the clavicles
options.zh: 颈椎固定——她有锁骨以上的明显损伤

options.en: No spinal care - an alert patient who is talking needs no precautions
options.zh: 不需脊柱处置——清醒且能说话的病人不需要保护

options.en: Wound packing - the laceration must be packed to control the bleeding
options.zh: 伤口填塞——裂伤必须填塞才能止血

questions.explanationEn: Obvious injury above the level of the clavicles is a BC indication for cervical spine stabilization in the primary survey (p.11), and her neck stiffness strengthens it. A is wrong because a forehead laceration in an alert, talking patient does not compromise the airway; obstructed-airway procedures are for absent respiration or inability to ventilate. C is wrong because alertness does not cancel the 'injury above the clavicles' indication. D is wrong because this bleeding is controlled with direct pressure; wound packing is reserved for junctional bleeding that direct pressure cannot control (p.19).
questions.explanationZh: 锁骨水平以上的明显损伤是 BC 初级评估中颈椎固定的指征之一（第 11 页），她的颈部僵硬感更支持这一点。A 错：清醒且能说话的病人，额头裂伤不会影响气道；气道梗阻处理的指征是无呼吸或无法通气。C 错：神志清楚并不能取消「锁骨以上损伤」这条指征。D 错：这种出血用直接压迫即可控制，伤口填塞只用于直接压迫无效的交界部位出血（第 19 页）。

questions.questionEn: A 90-year-old man with severe kyphosis requires spinal motion restriction after a fall down three stairs. When you lay him on the board his head hovers well above the surface and he cannot straighten. You should:
questions.questionZh: 一名严重驼背（kyphosis）的 90 岁男性从三级台阶上摔下，需要脊柱活动限制。把他放上脊柱板后，他的头部高高悬空，身体也无法伸直。你应该：

options.en: Press the head down to the board and secure it firmly with tape
options.zh: 把头压到板面上，用胶带牢牢固定

options.en: Omit spinal motion restriction, since kyphosis makes it impossible
options.zh: 放弃脊柱活动限制，驼背病人根本做不到

options.en: Pad under the head and shoulders to support him in his own neutral position
options.zh: 在头和肩下垫衬，按他自身的中立位加以支撑固定

options.en: Transport him prone so that the curve of his back faces upward
options.zh: 让他俯卧转运，使弯曲的背部朝上

questions.explanationEn: Spinal motion restriction means supporting the spine in the patient's own neutral alignment, not forcing it flat. Nancy recommends filling the voids between an older patient and the device with towel rolls or blankets and padding the board generously. A is wrong because forcing a rigid kyphotic spine straight can cause pain and fracture, and BC's spinal management guideline says not to tape the head (p.25). B is wrong because the deformity changes how you immobilize, not whether you do. D is wrong because prone positioning hinders airway monitoring and does not support his curvature.
questions.explanationZh: 脊柱活动限制的意思是把脊柱固定在病人自己的中立对线上，而不是强行压平。教材（Nancy）建议用毛巾卷或毯子填满老年病人与固定器材之间的空隙，并把脊柱板垫厚。A 错：强行压直僵硬的驼背可能造成疼痛和骨折，而且 BC 脊柱处置指南明确写着不要用胶带固定头部（第 25 页）。B 错：畸形改变的是固定方式，而不是要不要固定。D 错：俯卧不便监测气道，也撑不住他的脊柱弯曲。

questions.questionEn: A 76-year-old woman with CHF is in respiratory distress, sitting bolt upright at 0300, SpO2 88%. During the primary survey, which combination of survey interventions is indicated?
questions.questionZh: 凌晨 3 点，一名患充血性心衰（CHF）的 76 岁女性笔直端坐、呼吸窘迫，SpO2 88%。初级评估中应采取哪组干预？

options.en: Give oxygen, sit her upright with legs dangling, keep her at rest and warm
options.zh: 给氧，让她端坐、双腿下垂，保持静息和保暖

options.en: Lay her flat on the stretcher and cover her with a warm blanket
options.zh: 让她平躺在担架上，盖上保暖毯

options.en: Withhold oxygen until a full set of vital signs has been recorded
options.zh: 先记录完整的生命体征，再决定是否给氧

options.en: Place her semi-prone with oxygen by nasal cannula at 2 L/min
options.zh: 置于侧俯卧位，鼻导管 2 L/min 给氧

questions.explanationEn: Oxygen and position are both BC primary survey interventions (p.9, p.11): respiratory distress is an oxygen indication, and the CHF/pulmonary edema guideline (p.33) specifies sitting upright with the legs hung down, keeping the patient at rest and warm, and oxygen to SpO2 of 94% or higher. B is wrong because lying flat increases venous return and worsens pulmonary edema. C is wrong because oxygen is never delayed for vital signs in a hypoxic, distressed patient. D is wrong because semi-prone positioning is for patients who cannot protect their airway, and 2 L/min by cannula is inadequate for a short-of-breath patient at 88% - BC calls for high-flow oxygen when the patient is short of breath (p.50).
questions.explanationZh: 给氧和体位都是 BC 初级评估的干预项目（第 9、11 页）：呼吸窘迫是给氧指征，而充血性心衰/肺水肿（CHF/Pulmonary Edema）指南（第 33 页）要求让病人端坐、双腿下垂，保持静息和保暖，给氧维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%。B 错：平卧会增加回心血量，加重肺水肿。C 错：对缺氧且呼吸窘迫的病人，绝不能为了先测生命体征而推迟给氧。D 错：侧俯卧位（semi-prone）是给不能保护气道的病人的；气促、SpO2 88% 的病人用鼻导管 2 L/min 远远不够，BC 要求气促病人用高流量氧（第 50 页）。

questions.questionEn: A talkative 83-year-old woman called for her chronic knee pain, but as you assess her you notice she is speaking in shorter sentences than when you arrived and her breathing has become laboured with accessory muscle use. She insists she just wants to discuss her knee. You should:
questions.questionZh: 一名健谈的 83 岁女性因慢性膝痛呼叫救护。评估过程中你注意到，她说话的句子比你刚到时短了很多，呼吸变得费力，并出现辅助呼吸肌参与。她坚持只想谈膝盖的事。你应该：

options.en: Finish the knee assessment first, since it is her stated chief complaint
options.zh: 先做完膝部评估，那是她自述的主诉

options.en: Note the change and recheck her breathing after the knee examination
options.zh: 记下变化，膝部检查完再复查呼吸

options.en: Reassure her - long conversations often leave older patients breathless
options.zh: 安慰她——老年人说话一多常常会喘

options.en: Return to the primary survey - new respiratory distress takes priority
options.zh: 回到初级评估——新出现的呼吸窘迫优先处理

questions.explanationEn: Assessment is dynamic: whenever a new life threat appears, go back to the primary survey. Respiratory distress with accessory muscle use is a BC instability criterion (p.7) that calls for oxygen and a transport decision. A and B are wrong because they put a potential life threat behind a chronic complaint. C is wrong because accessory muscle use is never explained away as conversational breathlessness. Older patients often play down serious symptoms, so the crew's observations should set the priorities.
questions.explanationZh: 评估是动态的：一旦出现新的生命威胁，就要回到初级评估。呼吸窘迫伴辅助呼吸肌参与是 BC 不稳定标准之一（第 7 页），需要给氧并做转运决策。A 和 B 错在把可能危及生命的问题排在慢性主诉之后。C 错：辅助呼吸肌参与呼吸绝不能用「说话多了累的」来解释。老年人常常淡化严重症状，应以救护员的观察来决定优先次序。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.7, p.9; Nancy Ch 45

questions.questionEn: A 72-year-old man with a previous hip replacement felt his hip 'pop out' while bending; his leg is now shortened and internally rotated. Distal pulses are present. What does the BC guideline say about his transport category?
questions.questionZh: 一名做过髋关节置换的 72 岁男性弯腰时感到髋部「弹出」；患腿现在缩短并内旋，远端脉搏存在。BC 指南对他的转运分类怎么规定？

options.en: All hip dislocations are in the Rapid Transport Category
options.zh: 所有髋关节脱位都属于 Rapid Transport Category

options.en: Hip dislocations are rapid transport only when distal pulses are absent
options.zh: 只有远端脉搏消失的髋脱位才需要快速转运

options.en: Prosthetic hip dislocations are excluded from rapid transport rules
options.zh: 人工髋关节脱位不适用快速转运规则

options.en: He may wait for a scheduled transfer since this is a recurrent problem
options.zh: 这属于复发问题，可以等待预约转院

questions.explanationEn: The guideline states plainly: all hip dislocations are in the Rapid Transport Category, because early medical reduction is essential to avoid serious long-term complications. (Isolated hip fractures, by contrast, become rapid transport when there is neurovascular impairment.) Support the limb, secure to the stretcher, and monitor distal pulses en route.
questions.explanationZh: 指南明确写道：所有髋关节脱位都属于 Rapid Transport Category，因为早期医疗复位对避免严重长期并发症至关重要。（相比之下，孤立髋部骨折在有神经血管损害时才升为快速转运。）应支撑患肢、固定于担架，途中监测远端脉搏。

questions.questionEn: An 85-year-old woman fell and has an isolated suspected hip fracture: shortened, externally rotated left leg. Her left foot is cold and you cannot palpate the pedal pulse. This finding changes her management because:
questions.questionZh: 一名 85 岁女性跌倒后疑似孤立性髋部骨折：左腿缩短、外旋。她的左脚发凉，摸不到足背动脉搏动。这一发现为什么会改变她的处置？

options.en: No change - cool feet are common in older adults and expected
options.zh: 不需改变——老年人脚凉很常见，在意料之中

options.en: She now needs a traction splint to restore circulation
options.zh: 她现在需要用牵引夹板来恢复循环

options.en: Neurovascular compromise makes her hip fracture rapid transport
options.zh: 神经血管受损使她的髋部骨折升为快速转运

options.en: The absent pulse matters only if the skin is also mottled
options.zh: 只有皮肤同时出现花斑，脉搏消失才有意义

questions.explanationEn: BC states that isolated hip fractures become rapid transport if there is neurological or vascular impairment (p.22) - a cold, pulseless foot is exactly that. Quickly support the limb, secure her to a firm stretcher, transport rapidly, and recheck distal circulation frequently. A is wrong because a new cold, pulseless foot on the injured side is a finding, not a normal variant. B is wrong because traction splints are indicated for suspected mid-shaft femur fractures in stable patients (p.23), not hip fractures. D is wrong because an absent pulse is itself vascular impairment; mottling is not required.
questions.explanationZh: BC 规定，孤立的髋部骨折如有神经或血管损害即属快速转运（第 22 页）——脚凉、摸不到脉搏正是血管损害。应迅速支撑患肢，把她固定在硬质担架上快速转运，途中频繁复查远端循环。A 错：受伤一侧新出现的脚凉无脉是异常发现，不是正常变异。B 错：牵引夹板的指征是稳定病人疑似股骨干中段骨折（第 23 页），不是髋部骨折。D 错：脉搏消失本身就是血管损害，不需要再等花斑出现。

questions.questionEn: A 77-year-old man slipped from a standing position in his garage. On assessment his speech is newly slurred and his left hand grip is weaker than the right - his wife confirms both are new since the fall. Vitals are normal. Although the mechanism seems minor, he is categorized as:
questions.questionZh: 一名 77 岁男性在车库里站着时滑倒。评估发现他言语含糊、左手握力比右手弱——妻子确认这两点都是跌倒后才出现的。生命体征正常。尽管机制看似轻微，他应被归为：

options.en: Unstable - new neurological deficits are a criterion regardless of mechanism
options.zh: 不稳定——新发神经功能缺损本身就是标准，与机制无关

options.en: Stable - a fall from standing height never meets mechanism criteria
options.zh: 稳定——站立高度跌倒从不满足机制标准

options.en: Stable - his deficits are explained by a minor head bump from the fall
options.zh: 稳定——他的缺损可以用跌倒时轻微撞头来解释

options.en: Unstable only if his GCS falls below 13 during transport
options.zh: 只有转运途中 GCS 降到 13 以下才算不稳定

questions.explanationEn: New onset neurological deficits are a BC anatomical instability criterion, and suspected CVA is a primary survey instability criterion (p.7) - neither depends on mechanism. In an older patient, ask whether a medical event caused the fall: new slurred speech and unilateral weakness call for FAST-VAN assessment, a blood glucose check, timely transport, and notification en route (p.30). B is wrong because his instability comes from his findings, not the mechanism. C is wrong because attributing focal deficits to a trivial bump risks missing a stroke. D is wrong because GCS is not the trigger - new focal deficits already make him unstable.
questions.explanationZh: 新发神经功能缺损是 BC 解剖学不稳定标准，疑似脑血管意外（CVA）也是初级评估不稳定标准（第 7 页），两者都与受伤机制无关。对老年病人要追问是不是内科事件导致了跌倒：新出现的言语含糊和单侧无力，需要做 FAST-VAN 评估、测血糖、及时转运并在途中通知医院（第 30 页）。B 错：他的不稳定来自体征，而不是机制。C 错：把局灶性缺损归因于轻微碰撞，可能漏掉卒中。D 错：判定标准不是 GCS，新发局灶缺损本身就已构成不稳定。

questions.questionEn: An 87-year-old woman with moderate dementia is assessed after a fall. Her eyes are open spontaneously, she speaks in sentences but is disoriented to place and date, and she follows simple commands. Her GCS is:
questions.questionZh: 一名中度失智的 87 岁女性跌倒后接受评估。她自发睁眼，能成句说话，但对地点和日期定向障碍，能完成简单指令。她的 GCS 是：

options.en: GCS 15 - dementia is excluded from the verbal score
options.zh: GCS 15——失智不计入言语评分

options.en: GCS 12 - disorientation scores as inappropriate words
options.zh: GCS 12——定向障碍按不恰当词语计分

options.en: GCS 14 - interpret it against her known baseline
options.zh: GCS 14——要对照她已知的基线来解读

options.en: GCS cannot be scored in a patient with dementia
options.zh: 失智病人无法进行 GCS 评分

questions.explanationEn: Spontaneous eye opening is E4, confused (disoriented) conversation is V4, and obeying commands is M6: GCS 14. In dementia the number must be compared with her baseline - if she is always disoriented, 14 may be her normal; if she was oriented yesterday, the same 14 is an acute change. A is wrong because there is no dementia exception; disorientation lowers the verbal score. B is wrong because she speaks in sentences, which is confused conversation (V4), not inappropriate words (V3), and the total would not be 12 in any case. D is wrong because GCS can and should be scored; it simply needs context. Document both the score and the source of the baseline.
questions.explanationZh: 自发睁眼 E4，能交谈但定向混乱 V4，遵嘱动作 M6，合计 GCS 14。对失智病人，这个分数必须和基线比较——她平时就定向障碍的话，14 可能就是她的常态；如果她昨天还定向正常，同样的 14 就是急性变化。A 错：评分没有「失智除外」的规定，定向障碍就要扣言语分。B 错：她能成句说话，属于交谈混乱（V4）而不是不恰当词语（V3），而且无论如何总分都不是 12。D 错：失智病人可以也应该评 GCS，只是需要结合背景解读。分数和基线信息来源都要记录。

questions.questionEn: A 79-year-old man fell down a flight of stairs. He opens his eyes when you speak loudly, utters random inappropriate words, and localizes to a painful stimulus. What is his GCS and TBI classification?
questions.questionZh: 一名 79 岁男性从整段楼梯上摔下。你大声呼唤时他会睁眼，说出零散且不切题的词语，对疼痛刺激能定位。他的 GCS 和创伤性脑损伤（TBI）分级是什么？

options.en: GCS 13 - mild traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 13——轻度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 11 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 11——中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 9 - moderate traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 9——中度创伤性脑损伤

options.en: GCS 8 - severe traumatic brain injury
options.zh: GCS 8——重度创伤性脑损伤

questions.explanationEn: Eye opening to voice is E3, random inappropriate words V3, and localizing to pain M5: total 11, which BC classifies as moderate traumatic brain injury (9-12). A (13) would need confused conversation (V4) and obeying commands (M6), so it overscores. C (9) and D (8) underscore - for example by scoring localizing as withdrawal (M4) or the words as incomprehensible sounds (V2). Management follows the TBI guideline (p.27): SpO2 of 94% or higher, head of bed at 30 degrees, loosen the collar, and for PCPs maintain systolic BP above 120 mmHg. Reassess GCS frequently; a falling score matters more than any single value.
questions.explanationZh: 呼唤睁眼 E3，零散不切题的词语 V3，疼痛定位 M5，合计 11，BC 归为中度创伤性脑损伤（9–12）。A（13）需要交谈混乱（V4）且遵嘱动作（M6），属于评高了。C（9）和 D（8）则评低了，例如把疼痛定位当成回缩（M4），或把词语当成无法理解的声音（V2）。处理按创伤性脑损伤（TBI）指南（第 27 页）：维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%，床头抬高 30 度，松开颈托，PCP 还要维持收缩压 > 120 mmHg。要频繁复评 GCS，分数下降比任何单次数值都重要。

questions.questionEn: A 76-year-old woman with long-standing hypertension (usual BP around 165/95 per her home log) has vomited coffee-ground material. She is pale with HR 104. Her BP reads 118/76. How should you interpret this blood pressure?
questions.questionZh: 一名长期高血压的 76 岁女性（家庭记录显示平时血压约 165/95）呕吐咖啡渣样物。她面色苍白，HR 104，现测血压 118/76。你应如何解读这个血压？

options.en: Concerning - a large drop from her baseline; treat as relative hypotension
options.zh: 令人担忧——比她的基线下降很多，应按相对性低血压处理

options.en: Normal - a reading of 118/76 shows her volume status is adequate
options.zh: 正常——118/76 说明她的容量状态良好

options.en: Unreliable - her home log is probably inaccurate, so disregard it
options.zh: 不可靠——她的家庭记录可能不准，可以不予理会

options.en: Unreliable - automated cuffs often misread in older patients, so ignore it
options.zh: 不可靠——电子血压计对老年人常常测不准，应忽略此读数

questions.explanationEn: Nancy warns that a blood pressure that is normal for a younger person may mean hypotension in an older one, and that you should try to establish the patient's usual baseline. A drop from about 165 to 118 systolic - together with pallor, tachycardia, and coffee-ground emesis - signals significant volume loss. B is wrong because 'textbook normal' ignores her baseline. C is wrong because there is no evidence her log is wrong, and dismissing it removes your best comparator. D is wrong because a reading that fits the rest of the picture should not be discarded; if in doubt, repeat it manually. Manage as GI hemorrhage with hypovolemia (p.54): supine, warmth, oxygen, rapid transport, and PCP vascular access en route.
questions.explanationZh: 教材（Nancy）提醒：对年轻人正常的血压，对老年人可能就是低血压，应尽量了解病人平时的基线。收缩压从约 165 降到 118，再加上苍白、心动过速和咖啡渣样呕吐物，提示明显的容量丢失。B 错：所谓「教科书正常」忽略了她自己的基线。C 错：没有证据说明她的记录不准，丢掉它就失去了最好的对照。D 错：与整体表现吻合的读数不应丢弃，如有疑问可手动复测。应按消化道出血伴低血容量处理（第 54 页）：平卧、保暖、给氧、快速转运，PCP 在途中建立静脉通路。

questions.questionEn: An elderly patient reports feeling faint each time she stands up after starting a new diuretic. Which vital signs approach best evaluates this complaint?
questions.questionZh: 一名老年女性说，自从开始服用一种新的利尿剂，她每次站起来都觉得要晕倒。哪种生命体征评估方法最适合评估这一主诉？

options.en: Take one seated blood pressure and compare it with her usual reading
options.zh: 测一次坐位血压，与她平时的读数比较

options.en: Measure the blood pressure in both arms and compare the two sides
options.zh: 测双上肢血压并比较两侧

options.en: Check her SpO2 on standing, since dizziness on rising is usually hypoxic
options.zh: 站立时测 SpO2，起身头晕通常是缺氧所致

options.en: Compare lying and standing readings for a heart rate rise or systolic drop
options.zh: 比较卧位与站立位读数，看心率是否上升、收缩压是否下降

questions.explanationEn: Orthostatic (postural) vital signs compare supine with sitting or standing measurements and help gauge volume depletion. Nancy describes a positive test as a systolic fall of up to about 20 mmHg and a heart rate rise of about 20 beats/min, often with symptoms - common in older adults on diuretics. A is wrong because a single seated reading cannot show a positional change. B is wrong because arm-to-arm comparison looks for problems such as aortic dissection, not volume loss. C is wrong because dizziness on standing after starting a diuretic points to low volume, not hypoxia. Do the test only if the patient can stand safely, with the crew guarding against a fall.
questions.explanationZh: 体位性（orthostatic）生命体征是比较卧位与坐位或站立位的测量值，用来判断有无容量不足。教材（Nancy）描述的阳性标准是：收缩压下降约 20 mmHg、心率增加约 20 次/分，常伴症状——在服用利尿剂的老年人中很常见。A 错：一次坐位测量看不出体位变化。B 错：比较双臂血压是为了查主动脉夹层等问题，不是查容量不足。C 错：开始服利尿剂后一站起就头晕，指向的是容量不足而非缺氧。只有在病人能安全站立时才做这项检查，并由队员在旁防跌倒。

questions.questionEn: A 90-year-old man fainted at lunch. He takes metoprolol and digoxin. Now: HR 40 and regular, BP 88/54, he is pale and lightheaded. The most accurate clinical interpretation is:
questions.questionZh: 一名 90 岁男性午餐时晕倒。他服用美托洛尔（metoprolol）和地高辛（digoxin）。现在：HR 40 且规则，BP 88/54，面色苍白、头晕。最准确的临床判断是：

options.en: A rate of 40 is expected on metoprolol; reassure him and transport routinely
options.zh: 服美托洛尔心率 40 很正常；安慰他，常规转运即可

options.en: This is a vasovagal faint; observe on scene and release him if he improves
options.zh: 这是血管迷走性晕厥；现场观察，好转就不必转运

options.en: Symptomatic bradycardia with hypotension - unstable; O2, supine, prompt transport
options.zh: 症状性心动过缓伴低血压——不稳定；给氧、平卧、尽快转运

options.en: Sit him up and walk him to the stretcher to see if the dizziness persists
options.zh: 扶他坐起、走到担架旁，看头晕是否持续

questions.explanationEn: Syncope, a heart rate of 40, BP 88/54, and pallor together mean the slow rate is not perfusing him adequately - a symptomatic bradycardia, likely worsened by his beta blocker and digoxin (Nancy notes that such drugs can slow the heart excessively in older adults). He needs oxygen, supine positioning, prompt transport, and his medication list for the receiving team. A is wrong because hypotension and syncope make the rate dangerous regardless of the medication. B is wrong because a vasovagal faint does not explain persistent bradycardia and hypotension in a 90-year-old on rate-controlling drugs. D is wrong because standing a hypotensive patient risks another syncope and a fall.
questions.explanationZh: 晕厥、心率 40、血压 88/54、面色苍白放在一起，说明这么慢的心率已无法维持灌注——这是症状性心动过缓，很可能被他服用的美托洛尔（metoprolol）和地高辛（digoxin）加重（教材指出这类药可使老年人心率过度减慢）。他需要给氧、平卧、尽快转运，并把用药清单交给接收团队。A 错：已有低血压和晕厥，无论是否服药，这个心率都很危险。B 错：血管迷走性晕厥解释不了一位服控率药物的 90 岁老人持续的心动过缓和低血压。D 错：让低血压病人站起行走，可能再次晕厥并摔倒。

questions.questionEn: You are transporting an 81-year-old woman on apixaban who struck her head. Her GCS was 15 on scene; 20 minutes into transport she is drowsy, opening eyes to voice and now confused - GCS 13. The most appropriate response is to:
questions.questionZh: 你正在转运一名服用阿哌沙班（apixaban）、头部受撞的 81 岁女性。现场 GCS 15；转运 20 分钟后，她变得嗜睡，呼唤才睁眼，并出现意识混乱——GCS 13。最恰当的反应是：

options.en: Let her rest - drowsiness after a stressful event is to be expected
options.zh: 让她休息——经历应激事件后嗜睡是意料之中的

options.en: Treat the drop as a likely brain bleed: reassess ABCs, O2, head up, notify
options.zh: 按很可能的颅内出血处理：重评 ABC、给氧、抬高床头、通知医院

options.en: Record GCS 13 and carry on unchanged, since it is still 'mild' TBI
options.zh: 记录 GCS 13，其余照旧——这仍属「轻度」脑损伤

options.en: Give oral glucose first in case hypoglycemia explains the drowsiness
options.zh: 先给口服葡萄糖（oral glucose），以防嗜睡是低血糖引起的

questions.explanationEn: The direction of change matters more than the number: a two-point GCS drop in an anticoagulated older adult after a head strike signals an evolving intracranial bleed. Follow the BC TBI guideline (p.27): reassess ABCs, keep SpO2 at 94% or higher, elevate the head of the bed 30 degrees, and notify the receiving facility early. A is wrong because new drowsiness after a head injury is never 'just tiredness'. C is wrong because a GCS of 13 that was 15 twenty minutes ago is deterioration, whatever band it falls in. D is wrong because oral glucose requires a patient who can protect her airway and a measured low blood glucose; check the glucose, but do not delay brain-protective care on a guess.
questions.explanationZh: 变化方向比分数本身更重要：服抗凝药的老年人头部受撞后 GCS 下降 2 分，提示颅内出血正在进展。按 BC 创伤性脑损伤（TBI）指南（第 27 页）：重评 ABC，维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%，床头抬高 30 度，并尽早通知接收医院。A 错：头部受伤后新出现的嗜睡绝不能当成「累了」。C 错：20 分钟前还是 15 分的病人降到 13 分就是恶化，不论属于哪个分级。D 错：口服葡萄糖（oral glucose）要求病人能保护自己的气道并测得血糖低；可以测血糖，但不能凭猜测耽误脑保护处置。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.27; Nancy Ch 20, Ch 24

questions.questionEn: A 92-year-old woman with advanced dementia and a suspected femur fracture cannot answer the 0-10 pain scale. She is grimacing, guarding the leg, breathing at 28, and became agitated when moved. How should you assess and treat her pain?
questions.questionZh: 一名晚期失智的 92 岁女性疑似股骨骨折，无法回答 0–10 疼痛评分。她表情痛苦、护着患腿，呼吸 28 次/分，一搬动就躁动。你应如何评估和处理她的疼痛？

options.en: Document 'pain assessment not possible' and withhold analgesia
options.zh: 记录「无法评估疼痛」，不给镇痛

options.en: Assume dementia blunts pain and treat only if she cries out
options.zh: 假定失智使痛觉迟钝，只有她喊痛才处理

options.en: Ask repeatedly until she gives a 0-10 number you can record
options.zh: 反复追问，直到她说出一个可以记录的 0–10 数字

options.en: Use her behaviour as evidence of pain and give analgesia before moving her
options.zh: 把她的行为表现当作疼痛证据，在搬动前给予镇痛

questions.explanationEn: Dementia impairs the ability to report pain, not the injury that causes it. Behavioural and physiological cues - grimacing, guarding, agitation with movement, a raised respiratory rate - stand in for the numeric scale. BC's musculoskeletal guideline calls for analgesia prior to movement in stable, appropriate patients (p.21). A is wrong because an inability to self-report is not a reason to leave pain untreated. B is wrong because waiting for her to cry out ignores clear signs of pain she is already showing. C is wrong because a number forced from a patient who cannot use the scale is unreliable and distressing.
questions.explanationZh: 失智损害的是表达疼痛的能力，而不是造成疼痛的损伤本身。行为和生理线索——表情痛苦、护着患肢、一动就躁动、呼吸加快——可以代替数字评分。BC 骨骼肌肉损伤指南要求对稳定、合适的病人在搬动前给予镇痛（第 21 页）。A 错：无法自述疼痛不是不处理疼痛的理由。B 错：等她喊出来才处理，等于无视她已经表现出的疼痛信号。C 错：逼一个不会用评分表的病人报出的数字既不可靠，又徒增痛苦。

questions.questionEn: For a frail 84-year-old transfer patient you are asked to run the IV at the standard maintenance rate of 75 mL/hr using a micro-drip set (60 gtts/mL). What drip rate is that?
questions.questionZh: 一名体弱的 84 岁转院病人需要以标准维持速度 75 mL/hr 输液，使用微滴管（60 gtts/mL）。滴速应是多少？

options.en: 8 gtts/min
options.zh: 8 gtts/min

options.en: 13 gtts/min
options.zh: 13 gtts/min

options.en: 45 gtts/min
options.zh: 45 gtts/min

options.en: 75 gtts/min
options.zh: 75 gtts/min

questions.explanationEn: 75 mL x 60 gtts/mL / 60 minutes = 4500 / 60 = 75 gtts/min. With a 60 gtts/mL micro-drip set, gtts/min always equals mL/hr. 13 gtts/min is the answer for a 10 gtts/mL macro-drip set (75 x 10 / 60 = 12.5). 8 and 45 gtts/min come from using the wrong drop factor or dividing by the wrong time. The maintenance rate of about 75 mL/hr is the figure in BC's IV maintenance section (p.39).
questions.explanationZh: 75 mL × 60 gtts/mL ÷ 60 分钟 = 4500 ÷ 60 = 75 gtts/min。使用 60 gtts/mL 的微滴管时，gtts/min 的数值始终等于 mL/hr。13 gtts/min 是 10 gtts/mL 大滴管的答案（75 × 10 ÷ 60 = 12.5）。8 和 45 gtts/min 是用错滴系数或除错时间的结果。约 75 mL/hr 的维持速度正是 BC 静脉输液维持一节（第 39 页）给出的数值。

questions.questionEn: A 68-year-old woman (70 kg) with a history of CHF is hypotensive at 82/50 after two days of vomiting. The hypovolemia protocol allows a 20 mL/kg bolus to a maximum of 2 litres. What is the safest way to run this bolus?
questions.questionZh: 一名有充血性心衰（CHF）病史的 68 岁女性（70 kg）呕吐两天后血压 82/50。低血容量协议允许按 20 mL/kg、最多 2 升给予液体冲击。最安全的执行方式是什么？

options.en: Give it in 500 mL steps, rechecking lung sounds and breathing each time
options.zh: 分 500 mL 一段输注，每段后复查肺部听诊和呼吸

options.en: Run the full 1400 mL wide open without pausing, since the protocol allows it
options.zh: 协议允许，就一口气全速输完 1400 mL

options.en: Withhold fluid entirely, because CHF is an absolute contraindication
options.zh: 完全不补液，CHF 是绝对禁忌

options.en: Give 250 mL only, then switch to TKVO whatever her response
options.zh: 只给 250 mL，不论反应如何都改为保持静脉通畅（TKVO）

questions.explanationEn: Her calculated bolus is 20 mL/kg x 70 kg = 1400 mL. BC's hypovolemia and nausea-vomiting protocols both direct reassessment every 500 mL (p.48, p.54), and Nancy advises small boluses with frequent reassessment for pulmonary edema in older patients. In a CHF patient, auscultate for crackles and reassess work of breathing at each step, and stop if congestion develops; the nausea-vomiting protocol targets a systolic BP of 90 mmHg. B is wrong because running the full volume blind removes the protocol's safety check. C is wrong because CHF is not an absolute contraindication and she is clearly volume-depleted. D is wrong because an arbitrary 250 mL cap ignores her response - she may need more.
questions.explanationZh: 她的计算冲击量是 20 mL/kg × 70 kg = 1400 mL。BC 低血容量协议和恶心呕吐协议都要求每输 500 mL 重评一次（第 48、54 页），教材（Nancy）也建议老年人小量多次补液，并频繁评估有无肺水肿。对充血性心衰病人，每一段都要听诊有无湿啰音、重评呼吸做功，一旦出现肺淤血就停止；恶心呕吐协议的目标收缩压是 90 mmHg。B 错：盲目全速输完，等于去掉协议设定的安全检查。C 错：CHF 不是绝对禁忌，她明显容量不足。D 错：随意封顶 250 mL 忽略了病人的反应，她可能需要更多。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.48, p.54; Nancy Ch 45

questions.questionEn: The Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) allows a rapid 'from the doorway' impression of a sick child. What are its three arms?
questions.questionZh: 儿科评估三角（Pediatric Assessment Triangle, PAT）让你在门口第一眼就对患儿形成快速印象。它的三条边是什么？

options.en: Airway patency, blood pressure, and temperature
options.zh: 气道通畅度、血压和体温

options.en: Alertness, verbal response, and pain response
options.zh: 警觉程度、言语反应和疼痛反应

options.en: Appearance, work of breathing, and skin circulation
options.zh: 外观、呼吸做功和皮肤循环

options.en: Pulse rate, pupil response, and skin colour
options.zh: 脉率、瞳孔反应和肤色

questions.explanationEn: The Pediatric Assessment Triangle is a hands-off, from-the-doorway impression built on three elements: appearance (tone, interactiveness, consolability, look or gaze, speech or cry), work of breathing (abnormal sounds, positioning, retractions, flaring), and circulation to the skin (pallor, mottling, cyanosis). A is wrong because blood pressure and temperature need hands-on measurement and come later. B describes the AVPU scale, which belongs to the primary assessment. D lists hands-on findings (pulse, pupils) that also come after the general impression.
questions.explanationZh: 儿科评估三角（PAT）是不接触患儿、站在门口就能完成的总体印象，由三部分组成：外观（肌张力、互动、可安抚性、眼神、言语或哭声）、呼吸做功（异常呼吸音、体位、凹陷、鼻翼扇动）和皮肤循环（苍白、花斑、发绀）。A 错：血压和体温需要动手测量，属于后续步骤。B 描述的是 AVPU 意识评估，属于初级评估。D 列的脉搏、瞳孔也是动手检查的内容，在总体印象之后。

questions.questionEn: You enter a home to find an 18-month-old girl lying limp across her mother's lap. She makes no eye contact, does not resist your exam, and gives a weak intermittent whimper. Using PAT reasoning, this presentation indicates:
questions.questionZh: 你进门时看到一名 18 个月大的女孩软软地横躺在母亲腿上。她没有眼神接触，不抗拒你的检查，只发出微弱、断断续续的呜咽。按儿科评估三角（PAT）判断，这种表现提示：

options.en: A tired toddler who missed her nap; reassess after she has rested
options.zh: 错过午睡的疲倦幼儿；等她休息后再评估

options.en: Normal behaviour - quiet toddlers often warm up slowly to strangers
options.zh: 正常表现——安静的幼儿见到陌生人往往慢热

options.en: A well child, since she lets you examine her without a struggle
options.zh: 健康的孩子——她不挣扎、任由你检查

options.en: A seriously ill child - poor tone and no interaction are abnormal appearance
options.zh: 重症患儿——肌张力差、没有互动属于外观异常

questions.explanationEn: Appearance is the most important element of the PAT. A toddler who is limp, makes no eye contact, and does not resist examination has abnormal tone and interactiveness - signs of inadequate oxygenation, brain perfusion, or another serious derangement, whatever the eventual diagnosis. She needs a full primary assessment, oxygen as indicated, and prompt transport. A and B are wrong because they explain away abnormal appearance; a healthy 18-month-old with stranger anxiety cries and pulls away. C is wrong because, at this age, being 'easy to examine' is a red flag rather than reassurance.
questions.explanationZh: 外观是儿科评估三角（PAT）中最重要的一边。一个全身松软、没有眼神接触、也不抗拒检查的幼儿，肌张力和互动性都异常——无论最终诊断是什么，这都提示氧合不足、脑灌注不足或其他严重紊乱。她需要完整的初级评估、按指征给氧并尽快转运。A 和 B 错在为异常外观找借口：健康的 18 个月幼儿怕生时会哭闹、躲开。C 错：在这个年龄，「很好检查」是危险信号，而不是好消息。

questions.questionEn: When assessing for a pulse in an unresponsive infant, which site does the BC guideline direct you to use?
questions.questionZh: 评估无反应婴儿的脉搏时，BC 指南要求使用哪个部位？

options.en: Carotid artery
options.zh: 颈动脉

options.en: Radial artery
options.zh: 桡动脉

options.en: Brachial artery
options.zh: 肱动脉

options.en: Dorsalis pedis artery
options.zh: 足背动脉

questions.explanationEn: The infant CPR basics state: assess for a pulse using the brachial rather than the carotid artery. An infant's short, chubby neck makes the carotid difficult and unreliable to palpate; the brachial site on the inner upper arm is accessible and accurate.
questions.explanationZh: 婴儿 CPR 基础要点指出：应触诊肱动脉而非颈动脉。婴儿脖颈短而多肉，颈动脉难以可靠触及；上臂内侧的肱动脉既好找又准确。
