questions.questionEn: Why does the BC guideline recommend placing a pad under an infant's shoulders during CPR or airway management?
questions.questionZh: 为什么 BC 指南建议在为婴儿做 CPR 或气道管理时在其肩下垫东西？

options.en: To offset the large head, which flexes the neck when the infant lies flat
options.zh: 抵消头部偏大造成的影响——婴儿平躺时颈部会前屈

options.en: To raise the chest so that compressions can reach full depth
options.zh: 抬高胸部，使按压能达到足够深度

options.en: To tilt the head into maximal extension to open the airway
options.zh: 让头部最大限度后仰，以打开气道

options.en: To keep the infant's back off a cold surface during resuscitation
options.zh: 复苏时让婴儿背部离开冰冷的地面

questions.explanationEn: BC's infant/child CPR basics (p.43) explain that, because of the size of an infant's head relative to the body, a pad under the shoulders helps achieve a neutral position. Lying flat pushes the neck into flexion and can obstruct the soft infant airway. B is wrong because the pad aligns the airway; it does not change compression depth. C is wrong because the goal is a neutral position, not maximal extension - overextension can also kink an infant's airway. D is wrong because, although warmth matters, it is not the reason for the shoulder pad.
questions.explanationZh: BC 婴儿/儿童 CPR 要点（第 43 页）说明：由于婴儿头部相对身体偏大，在肩下垫一块垫子有助于维持中立位。平躺时颈部会被推成前屈，可能压闭柔软的婴儿气道。B 错：垫子是为了对齐气道，与按压深度无关。C 错：目标是中立位而不是最大后仰——过度后仰同样会让婴儿气道打折。D 错：保暖固然重要，但不是肩下垫物的原因。

questions.questionEn: You and your partner are performing CPR on an 8-month-old infant. What compression-to-ventilation ratio should you use?
questions.questionZh: 你和搭档两人正在为一名 8 个月大的婴儿做 CPR。应采用什么按压通气比？
questions.explanationEn: BC's infant/child guideline (p.41, p.43) uses 30:2 for one rescuer and 15:2 for two rescuers. With you and your partner both performing CPR on an 8-month-old, 15:2 applies; the extra ventilations reflect the mainly asphyxial cause of pediatric arrest. A (30:2) is the one-rescuer infant ratio and the adult ratio. C (3:1) is reserved for neonates up to 28 days. D (5:1) is not a BC ratio. Compress at 100-120 per minute to one-third to one-half of the chest depth.
questions.explanationZh: BC 婴儿/儿童指南（第 41、43 页）规定：单人施救 30:2，双人施救 15:2。你和搭档两人为一名 8 个月婴儿做 CPR，应采用 15:2；通气比例更高，对应儿童骤停多由窒息引起的特点。A（30:2）是婴儿单人施救和成人的比例。C（3:1）只用于出生 28 天内的新生儿。D（5:1）不是 BC 的比例。按压频率每分钟 100–120 次，深度为胸廓前后径的 1/3 至 1/2。

questions.questionEn: A 4-month-old with bronchiolitis is mottled and barely responsive. The brachial pulse is present but slow - you count 50 beats per minute. Breathing is shallow and gasping. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一名患毛细支气管炎的 4 个月婴儿皮肤花斑、几乎没有反应。肱动脉搏动存在但很慢——每分钟 50 次。呼吸浅、呈喘息样。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Ventilate only, since compressions are not given while a pulse is present
options.zh: 只做通气——有脉搏时不做胸外按压

options.en: Give oxygen by mask and recheck the pulse in 2 minutes
options.zh: 面罩给氧，2 分钟后复查脉搏

options.en: Begin CPR - a rate below 60 with poor perfusion is treated as arrest
options.zh: 开始 CPR——心率低于 60 且灌注不良按骤停处理

options.en: Apply the AED and analyze before starting any compressions
options.zh: 先贴 AED 分析心律，再决定是否按压

questions.explanationEn: BC's child/infant CPR guideline (p.41, p.43) directs CPR if there is no pulse or if the heart rate is below 60 with signs of poor perfusion - pallor, mottling, cyanosis, decreasing level of consciousness. A 4-month-old with a rate of 50, mottling, near-unresponsiveness, and gasping meets this. A is wrong because a palpable pulse below 60 with poor perfusion is an indication for compressions, not a contraindication. B is wrong because gasping respirations need ventilation, and delaying CPR allows arrest. D is wrong because the AED should not delay compressions; in pediatric arrest, ventilation and compressions address the usual asphyxial cause.
questions.explanationZh: BC 儿童/婴儿 CPR 指南（第 41、43 页）规定：无脉搏，或心率低于 60 且有灌注不良表现（苍白、花斑、发绀、意识下降）时，就开始 CPR。这名 4 个月婴儿心率 50、皮肤花斑、几乎无反应、喘息样呼吸，完全符合。A 错：能摸到脉搏但心率低于 60 且灌注不良，是按压的指征而不是禁忌。B 错：喘息样呼吸需要通气，拖延 CPR 会让孩子进入心搏骤停。D 错：AED 不应推迟按压；儿童骤停多由窒息引起，通气和按压才针对病因。

questions.questionEn: Off duty and without a phone, you find a 3-year-old unresponsive and pulseless at a playground. Nobody saw what happened and you are alone. What does the guideline direct?
questions.questionZh: 你下班后没带手机，在游乐场发现一名 3 岁儿童无反应、无脉搏。无人目击发生经过，现场只有你一个人。指南要求怎么做？

options.en: Leave the child to find a phone, then return to start CPR
options.zh: 先离开去找电话，回来再开始 CPR

options.en: Give about 2 minutes (5 cycles) of CPR, then go for help and an AED
options.zh: 先做约 2 分钟（5 个循环）CPR，再去求助并取 AED

options.en: Give rescue breaths only until someone happens to arrive
options.zh: 只做人工呼吸，直到碰巧有人经过

options.en: Continue CPR for 10 minutes before considering leaving the child
options.zh: 先做 10 分钟 CPR，再考虑离开孩子

questions.explanationEn: For an unwitnessed collapse when you are alone, BC's infant/child guideline (p.43) directs 5 cycles (about 2 minutes) of CPR before activating the emergency response system and getting an AED, because pediatric arrests are usually asphyxial and immediate CPR addresses the cause. A is wrong because leaving first delays oxygen delivery to a child who most likely arrested from hypoxia. C is wrong because a pulseless child needs compressions as well as breaths. D is wrong because the guideline sets about 2 minutes, not 10, before getting help. Had the collapse been witnessed, you would activate the system and get an AED immediately.
questions.explanationZh: 单人遇到无人目击的儿童倒地时，BC 婴儿/儿童指南（第 43 页）要求先做 5 个循环（约 2 分钟）CPR，再启动急救系统并取 AED，因为儿童骤停大多由窒息引起，立即 CPR 针对的正是病因。A 错：先离开会推迟给一个很可能因缺氧而骤停的孩子供氧。C 错：无脉搏的孩子除了人工呼吸还需要胸外按压。D 错：指南规定的是约 2 分钟，而不是 10 分钟。如果倒地有人目击，则应立即启动急救系统并取 AED。

questions.questionEn: A 12-year-old is struck in the centre of the chest by a line drive at a baseball game and collapses immediately in front of a crowd. You are first on scene with a bystander beside you. Why does this situation demand the AED as early as possible?
questions.questionZh: 棒球比赛中，一名 12 岁少年胸部正中被平飞球击中，随即在众人面前倒地。你第一个到场，身边有一名旁观者。为什么这种情况要求尽早使用 AED？

options.en: All pediatric arrests are shockable, so the AED takes priority over CPR
options.zh: 儿童骤停都是可电击心律，AED 优先于 CPR

options.en: The AED is needed mainly to record the rhythm for the hospital
options.zh: AED 主要是为医院记录心律

options.en: Once the AED is applied, chest compressions are no longer necessary
options.zh: 贴上 AED 以后就不用再做胸外按压

options.en: A chest blow then collapse suggests commotio cordis, where VF is likely
options.zh: 胸部受击后倒地提示心脏震荡，很可能是室颤

questions.explanationEn: Most pediatric arrests are asphyxial, but BC (p.44) notes that ventricular fibrillation does occur in children with previous cardiac problems, electrocution, or a sharp blow to the precordium followed by collapse (commotio cordis). This witnessed sudden collapse fits that pattern, so early defibrillation is decisive: start CPR and send the bystander for the AED (for a witnessed collapse, activate the system and get an AED immediately, p.43). A is wrong because most pediatric arrests are not shockable. B is wrong because the AED's purpose is defibrillation, not documentation. C is wrong because compressions and defibrillation coexist - CPR resumes immediately after each shock.
questions.explanationZh: 儿童心搏骤停大多由窒息引起，但 BC 考纲（第 44 页）指出：有心脏病史、触电，或心前区被猛击后倒地（心脏震荡，commotio cordis）的儿童可能发生室颤。这次被目击的突然倒地正符合这一模式，早期除颤起决定作用：你开始 CPR，让旁观者去取 AED（目击倒地应立即启动急救系统并取 AED，第 43 页）。A 错：大多数儿童骤停并不是可电击心律。B 错：AED 的作用是除颤，不是记录心律。C 错：按压和除颤并行，每次电击后要立即恢复 CPR。

questions.questionEn: You record a heart rate of 130 and a respiratory rate of 38 in a settled 6-month-old with a mild fever. How should you interpret these numbers?
questions.questionZh: 你为一名安静、低热的 6 个月婴儿测得心率 130 次/分、呼吸 38 次/分。应如何解读？

options.en: Both fall within the expected range for a 6-month-old infant
options.zh: 两项都在 6 个月婴儿的正常范围内

options.en: Both are dangerously high and indicate decompensated shock
options.zh: 两项都危险偏高，提示失代偿性休克

options.en: The heart rate is normal, but the respiratory rate indicates respiratory failure
options.zh: 心率正常，但呼吸频率提示呼吸衰竭

options.en: Both are too low for this age and suggest impending arrest
options.zh: 对这个年龄来说两项都偏低，提示即将骤停

questions.explanationEn: Nancy's pediatric reference ranges give an awake infant (1 month to 1 year) a heart rate of about 100-180 beats/min and a respiratory rate of about 30-53 breaths/min, so 130 and 38 in a settled, mildly febrile 6-month-old are both normal. B is wrong because neither value is high for this age, and decompensated shock would come with poor appearance and perfusion. C is wrong because 38 is within the infant range, not respiratory failure. D is wrong because neither value is low for an infant; the infant danger threshold is a heart rate below 60 with poor perfusion, which calls for CPR (BC p.43). Applying adult norms to infants is a classic error in both directions.
questions.explanationZh: 教材（Nancy）的儿科参考值中，清醒婴儿（1 个月至 1 岁）心率约 100–180 次/分，呼吸约 30–53 次/分，所以一名安静、低热的 6 个月婴儿心率 130、呼吸 38 都属正常。B 错：这两个数值在该年龄都不算高，失代偿性休克还会伴有外观和灌注异常。C 错：38 次/分在婴儿正常范围内，不是呼吸衰竭。D 错：这两个数值对婴儿来说都不低；婴儿的危险阈值是心率低于 60 且灌注不良，此时需要开始 CPR（BC 第 43 页）。把成人标准套到婴儿身上，往哪个方向都会判错。

questions.questionEn: A 2-year-old with a two-day history of vomiting and diarrhea is alert but quiet. His hands are cool and mottled to the wrists, capillary refill is 4 seconds, and the radial pulse is weak but present. His blood pressure is 92/60. What does this picture indicate?
questions.questionZh: 一名 2 岁儿童呕吐、腹泻两天，神志清楚但很安静。双手至腕部发凉、有花斑，毛细血管再充盈 4 秒，桡动脉搏动微弱但可触及，血压 92/60。这些表现提示什么？

options.en: Adequate perfusion - a normal blood pressure excludes shock in a child
options.zh: 灌注充足——儿童血压正常即可排除休克

options.en: Mild dehydration only - he can be managed with oral fluids at home
options.zh: 只是轻度脱水——在家口服补液即可

options.en: Cold exposure - mottling and cool hands are environmental findings
options.zh: 受凉——花斑和手凉是环境因素造成的

options.en: Compensated shock - skin signs worsen before blood pressure falls in children
options.zh: 代偿性休克——儿童皮肤征象恶化早于血压下降

questions.explanationEn: Children maintain blood pressure through vasoconstriction and tachycardia far longer than adults, so the circulation-to-skin findings - cool, mottled hands to the wrists and capillary refill of 4 seconds (Nancy gives normal as under 3) - become abnormal while the blood pressure is still normal. For a 2-year-old the minimum acceptable systolic is 70 + (2 x age) = 74 mmHg, so 92 is normal. A is wrong because compensated shock exists with a normal BP; once it falls, the child is decompensating. B is wrong because two days of losses with poor perfusion is beyond home oral rehydration. C is wrong because mottling can be a cold response, but with delayed refill, a weak pulse, and ongoing fluid loss it must be treated as poor perfusion.
questions.explanationZh: 儿童靠血管收缩和心率增快维持血压的时间远长于成人，所以皮肤循环表现——双手至腕部发凉、花斑，毛细血管再充盈 4 秒（教材给的正常值是 3 秒以内）——在血压仍正常时就已异常。2 岁儿童的最低可接受收缩压为 70 + 2 × 年龄 = 74 mmHg，92 属正常。A 错：代偿性休克时血压可以正常，等血压下降时孩子已经失代偿。B 错：丢液两天又已灌注不良，不能靠在家口服补液解决。C 错：花斑可能是受凉反应，但伴有再充盈延迟、脉搏微弱和持续丢液时，必须按灌注不良处理。

questions.questionEn: A 20 kg child is hypotensive after significant blood loss. Using the BC fluid bolus of 20 mL/kg, what volume should you plan for the first bolus?
questions.questionZh: 一名 20 kg 儿童明显失血后出现低血压。按 BC 20 mL/kg 的液体冲击量，第一次冲击应计划输入多少？

options.en: 400 mL
options.zh: 400 mL

options.en: 200 mL
options.zh: 200 mL

options.en: 2000 mL, the protocol maximum
options.zh: 2000 mL——协议上限

questions.explanationEn: 20 mL/kg x 20 kg = 400 mL (hypovolemia protocol, p.54). B (200 mL) is a 10 mL/kg dose - half the BC bolus. C (1000 mL) has no basis in the weight calculation. D (2000 mL) is the protocol's maximum cap, not a dose; for a 20 kg child it would be 100 mL/kg, a five-fold overdose. Reassess after the bolus - in a small child the full bolus is reached long before the 500 mL reassessment mark.
questions.explanationZh: 20 mL/kg × 20 kg = 400 mL（低血容量协议，第 54 页）。B（200 mL）是 10 mL/kg，只有 BC 冲击量的一半。C（1000 mL）在体重计算上毫无依据。D（2000 mL）是协议的封顶上限，不是剂量；给 20 kg 儿童相当于 100 mL/kg，是五倍过量。冲击后要重新评估——小体重儿童远在输到 500 mL 的重评节点之前就已输完整个冲击量。

questions.questionEn: A frightened 4-year-old with a forearm injury screams and pulls away whenever you approach. Which approach best allows you to complete an accurate assessment?
questions.questionZh: 一名前臂受伤、受了惊吓的 4 岁男孩，你一靠近他就尖叫躲闪。哪种做法最有利于完成准确的评估？

options.en: Have two crew members hold him still so the exam is quick
options.zh: 让两名队员按住他，尽快查完

options.en: Separate him from the parent to reduce distraction and fear
options.zh: 把他和家长分开，减少干扰和恐惧

options.en: Examine at his eye level on the caregiver's lap, injured arm last
options.zh: 让他坐在照护者腿上，平视检查，受伤的手臂放到最后

options.en: Skip the hands-on exam and rely on the parent's description
options.zh: 不做体格检查，只靠家长描述

questions.explanationEn: Nancy advises examining a young child in stable condition on the caregiver's lap, getting down to the child's level, using play and distraction, and leaving the most upsetting parts - such as examining an injured extremity - until last. This keeps the child calmer and the findings more reliable. A is wrong because restraining a frightened child produces struggling and unreliable findings; restraint is reserved for immediate safety needs. B is wrong because separating a young child from the caregiver increases fear and reduces cooperation. D is wrong because the injured limb still needs a hands-on check of circulation, sensation, and movement.
questions.explanationZh: 教材（Nancy）建议：情况稳定的幼儿可以坐在照护者腿上接受检查，救护员蹲到孩子的高度，利用游戏和分散注意力，把最让孩子难受的部分——如检查受伤肢体——放到最后。这样孩子更平静，检查结果也更可靠。A 错：按住受惊的孩子只会让他挣扎，结果不可靠，强制约束只用于即刻的安全需要。B 错：把幼儿和照护者分开会加重恐惧、降低配合度。D 错：受伤的手臂仍需要亲手检查远端循环、感觉和活动。

questions.questionEn: A 5-year-old with severe asthma has been working hard to breathe for an hour. Over ten minutes his respiratory rate falls from 44 to 18, his wheeze becomes quiet, and he stops fighting the oxygen mask. What does this change mean?
questions.questionZh: 一名 5 岁重度哮喘患儿已经费力呼吸了一个小时。十分钟内，他的呼吸频率从 44 降到 18，哮鸣音变轻，也不再抗拒氧气面罩。这种变化意味着什么？

options.en: Impending respiratory failure - he is tiring and needs assisted breaths
options.zh: 即将呼吸衰竭——他已力竭，需要辅助通气

options.en: The salbutamol is working and his bronchospasm is resolving
options.zh: 沙丁胺醇（salbutamol）起效了，支气管痉挛正在缓解

options.en: He is simply falling asleep after exhausting himself crying
options.zh: 他只是哭累了，正在入睡

options.en: His work of breathing has eased, so the oxygen can now be weaned
options.zh: 呼吸做功减轻了，可以开始撤氧

questions.explanationEn: In an asthmatic child, a falling respiratory rate, a quieter chest, and decreasing responsiveness signal exhaustion and impending respiratory failure, not improvement - air movement has become too poor to produce a wheeze. Nancy lists decreased retractions from fatigue, altered mental status, and an abnormally low respiratory rate as signs of respiratory failure, and BC's primary survey indications include assisting respirations that are abnormally slow or shallow with decreasing LOC (p.11). B is wrong because true improvement comes with better air entry and a more alert child. C is wrong because 'falling asleep' with a slowing rate is a decreasing LOC. D is wrong because removing oxygen from a tiring, hypoxic child could precipitate arrest.
questions.explanationZh: 哮喘患儿出现呼吸频率下降、胸部变「安静」、反应变差，是力竭和即将呼吸衰竭的信号，而不是好转——气流已经弱到发不出哮鸣音。教材（Nancy）把因疲劳而凹陷减轻、意识改变和呼吸频率异常偏低列为呼吸衰竭的表现；BC 初级评估干预指征也包括：呼吸异常缓慢或表浅并伴意识下降时应辅助通气（第 11 页）。B 错：真正的好转是进气改善、孩子更清醒。C 错：呼吸变慢时的「睡着」就是意识下降。D 错：给一个正在力竭、缺氧的孩子撤氧可能诱发骤停。

questions.questionEn: How long may suction be applied in a pediatric patient and in an infant according to the BC guidelines?
questions.questionZh: 根据 BC 指南，儿童和婴儿的每次吸痰时间上限分别是多少？

options.en: 10 seconds in the pediatric patient and 5 seconds in an infant
options.zh: 儿童 10 秒，婴儿 5 秒

options.en: 15 seconds in the pediatric patient and 10 seconds in an infant
options.zh: 儿童 15 秒，婴儿 10 秒

options.en: 20 seconds in the pediatric patient and 15 seconds in an infant
options.zh: 儿童 20 秒，婴儿 15 秒

options.en: 5 seconds in the pediatric patient and 3 seconds in an infant
options.zh: 儿童 5 秒，婴儿 3 秒

questions.explanationEn: The guideline specifies 10-15 seconds in the adult, 10 seconds in the pediatric patient, and 5 seconds in an infant. Shorter times reflect smaller oxygen reserves and higher metabolic demand - prolonged suctioning causes hypoxia and bradycardia in small children.
questions.explanationZh: 指南规定：成人 10-15 秒，儿童 10 秒，婴儿 5 秒。时间更短是因为氧储备更小、代谢需求更高——吸引时间过长会使幼儿出现低氧和心动过缓。

questions.questionEn: A conscious 9-month-old choked on a grape. He cannot cry or cough and is turning blue. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一名 9 个月大的清醒婴儿被葡萄噎住，无法哭也无法咳嗽，面色发绀。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Perform abdominal thrusts as you would for an adult
options.zh: 像对成人一样做腹部冲击

options.en: Perform a blind finger sweep to retrieve the grape
options.zh: 用手指盲掏，把葡萄取出来

options.en: Encourage him to cough forcefully and monitor closely
options.zh: 鼓励他用力咳嗽并密切观察

options.en: Give cycles of 5 back blows then 5 chest compressions
options.zh: 反复给予 5 次拍背加 5 次胸部按压的循环

questions.explanationEn: For an infant with a complete obstruction the guideline directs repeated cycles of 5 back blows followed by 5 chest compressions. Abdominal thrusts are described for conscious adults and children over 1 year of age, not infants. Blind finger sweeps are explicitly prohibited, and encouraging coughing applies only to a partial obstruction where the infant can still move air.
questions.explanationZh: 对完全气道梗阻的婴儿，指南要求反复循环给予 5 次拍背和 5 次胸部按压。腹部冲击适用于清醒的成人和 1 岁以上儿童，不适用于婴儿。盲目手指清扫被明确禁止；鼓励咳嗽只适用于仍有气流的部分梗阻。

questions.questionEn: You are resuscitating a 5-year-old in cardiac arrest and your AED kit contains only adult pads. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你正在为一名 5 岁心搏骤停患儿实施复苏，AED 套件里只有成人电极片。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Do not use the AED at all - adult pads are contraindicated under 8 years of age
options.zh: 完全不用 AED——8 岁以下禁用成人电极片

options.en: Use the adult pads and deliver the adult joules
options.zh: 使用成人电极片并按成人能量除颤

options.en: Cut the adult pads in half to reduce the delivered energy
options.zh: 把成人电极片剪成一半以减少输出能量

options.en: Wait for another unit to arrive with pediatric pads before analyzing
options.zh: 等另一辆车送来儿科电极片后再分析心律

questions.explanationEn: The guideline states that for a child 0-8 years switch to child AED pads if available, and if not available you may use the adult pads and deliver the adult joules. Delaying or withholding defibrillation is far more harmful than a slightly higher energy dose. Never modify pads.
questions.explanationZh: 指南规定：0-8 岁儿童如有儿科电极片则更换使用，若没有，可以使用成人电极片并给予成人能量。延误或放弃除颤的危害远大于稍高的能量剂量。绝不可裁剪或改造电极片。

questions.questionEn: Placing AED pads on a small 2-year-old in arrest, you see that in the standard anterior/lateral position the two pads are almost touching - about 2 cm apart. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 为一名体型瘦小的 2 岁骤停患儿贴 AED 电极片时，你发现按标准前/侧位放置后两片几乎相碰——间距约 2 cm。你应该怎么做？

options.en: Leave them as placed, since this is the standard position
options.zh: 维持原位——这是标准位置

options.en: Overlap the pads so both make full skin contact
options.zh: 让两片重叠，确保都贴紧皮肤

options.en: Move them to an anterior/posterior position
options.zh: 改为前/后位放置

options.en: Trim one pad so that it fits beside the other
options.zh: 剪小其中一片，让两片能并排放下

questions.explanationEn: The guideline states that if pads in the normal anterior/lateral chest position are within 2.5 cm (one inch) of each other, they may need to be shifted to an anterior/posterior configuration. Leaving them as placed (A) or overlapping them (B) allows current to arc between the pads across the skin rather than through the heart. Trimming a pad (D) damages it and is never appropriate.
questions.explanationZh: 考纲规定：若按常规前/侧位放置时两片间距在 2.5 cm（1 英寸）以内，可能需要改为前/后位放置。维持原位（A）或让两片重叠（B），电流会沿皮肤在两片之间「短路」，而不是穿过心脏。剪小电极片（D）会损坏电极，任何情况下都不可取。

questions.questionEn: You are managing a 3-year-old in cardiac arrest after a drowning. CPR is in progress. Regarding intra-arrest transport, which statement reflects the BC guideline?
questions.questionZh: 你正在处理一名溺水后心搏骤停的 3 岁儿童，CPR 正在进行。关于「骤停中转运」，哪种说法符合 BC 指南？

options.en: Transport with ongoing CPR is never permitted, because compressions deteriorate in motion
options.zh: 绝不允许边做 CPR 边转运，因为行进中按压质量会下降

options.en: Moving with CPR may occur for pediatric, hypothermic, traumatic, or treatable-cause arrests
options.zh: 儿科、低体温、创伤或可逆病因的骤停，可以边做 CPR 边转运

options.en: A pediatric arrest must be worked on scene for 30 minutes before any movement
options.zh: 儿童骤停必须在现场做满 30 分钟才能搬动

options.en: Every arrest should be transported immediately to reach definitive care sooner
options.zh: 所有骤停都应立即转运，以便尽快获得确定性治疗

questions.explanationEn: BC (p.42) acknowledges that CPR is more effective while stationary, but lists paediatrics, hypothermia, trauma, and treatable causes as situations in which intra-arrest transport with ongoing CPR may occur. A drowning arrest in a 3-year-old is both pediatric and hypoxic - hypoxia is a listed treatable cause (p.45). A is wrong because the guideline explicitly allows these exceptions. C is wrong because the 30-minute figure comes from the adult termination guidance (p.40) and is not a requirement to stay on scene with a child. D is wrong because for most arrests CPR is better delivered on scene; immediate transport is not the default.
questions.explanationZh: BC 考纲（第 42 页）承认静止状态下的 CPR 效果更好，但列出了可以边做 CPR 边转运的情形：儿科、低体温、创伤和可逆病因。3 岁儿童溺水后骤停，既属于儿科，又是缺氧所致——缺氧是列明的可逆病因（第 45 页）。A 错：指南明确允许这些例外。C 错：30 分钟出自成人 CPR 的终止条件（第 40 页），并不是要求儿童必须在现场做满 30 分钟。D 错：大多数骤停在现场做 CPR 效果更好，立即转运不是默认做法。

questions.questionEn: A 2-year-old with a febrile illness lies still. He does not open his eyes when his mother calls him, but he cries and pulls his hand away when you press firmly on his nail bed. Using AVPU, he is:
questions.questionZh: 一名发热的 2 岁男孩安静地躺着。母亲叫他时他不睁眼，但你用力按压他的甲床时，他哭了起来并把手抽回。按 AVPU 评估，他属于：

options.en: V - crying counts as a verbal response
options.zh: V——哭声算作言语反应

options.en: A - pulling away is a purposeful, alert response
options.zh: A——抽回手是有目的的清醒反应

options.en: P - he responds only to a painful stimulus
options.zh: P——只对疼痛刺激有反应

options.en: U - AVPU cannot be applied to a toddler
options.zh: U——幼儿不能用 AVPU 评估

questions.explanationEn: Response only to a painful stimulus is P at any age; crying triggered by nail-bed pressure is a response to pain, not to voice. BC's AVPU table (p.13) says a patient at P must have the airway monitored closely with intervention as necessary, and should be semi-prone, injuries permitting. A is wrong because he did not respond to his mother's voice - the cry followed the pain. B is wrong because 'alert' means awake and interacting without stimulation. D is wrong because AVPU is used for patients of any age, including children (Nancy Ch 44). A toddler who does not respond to a parent's voice is seriously ill.
questions.explanationZh: 只对疼痛刺激有反应，无论年龄都评为 P；按压甲床后引发的哭闹是对疼痛的反应，不是对声音的反应。BC 的 AVPU 表（第 13 页）要求：P 级病人必须严密监测气道、按需干预，损伤允许时应取侧俯卧位（semi-prone）。A 错：他对母亲的呼唤没有反应，哭是在疼痛之后才出现的。B 错：A（alert）指不需要刺激就清醒、能互动。D 错：AVPU 适用于任何年龄，包括儿童（教材第 44 章）。幼儿对父母的呼唤毫无反应，说明病情严重。

questions.questionEn: A 9-year-old with pneumonia has an SpO2 of 90% on oxygen, a respiratory rate of 34, and accessory muscle use. He is awake and following commands. Can you apply CPAP?
questions.questionZh: 一名 9 岁肺炎患儿吸氧下 SpO2 90%，呼吸 34 次/分，有辅助呼吸肌参与，清醒且能遵嘱。可以给他用持续气道正压（CPAP）吗？

options.en: Yes - he meets the respiratory rate, SpO2, and accessory muscle criteria
options.zh: 可以——他符合呼吸频率、SpO2 和辅助呼吸肌三项标准

options.en: Yes, provided the pressure is kept at 5 cmH2O
options.zh: 可以，只要压力保持在 5 cmH2O

options.en: No - CPAP is contraindicated at 12 years of age and under
options.zh: 不可以——12 岁及以下禁用 CPAP

options.en: Yes - pneumonia is a listed CPAP indication at any age
options.zh: 可以——肺炎在任何年龄都是 CPAP 的适应证

questions.explanationEn: BC's CPAP guideline (p.52) applies to patients 13 years of age and older and lists 'patient 12 years and less' as a contraindication. That overrides the fact that he meets the RR > 24, SpO2 < 94% on oxygen, and accessory muscle criteria (A), and that pneumonia is otherwise a listed indication (D). B is wrong because a lower pressure does not remove an age contraindication. Support him with titrated oxygen, and assist ventilations with a BVM if he tires.
questions.explanationZh: BC 持续气道正压（CPAP）指南（第 52 页）适用于 13 岁及以上病人，并把「12 岁及以下」列为禁忌。所以即使他符合呼吸 > 24、吸氧下 SpO2 < 94%、辅助呼吸肌参与这几项（A），肺炎本身也在适应证中（D），仍然不能用。B 错：压力调低并不能消除年龄禁忌。应滴定给氧，若他体力不支则用球囊面罩（BVM）辅助通气。

questions.questionEn: You must deliver a 300 mL fluid bolus to a 15 kg child over 20 minutes using a 10 gtts/mL set. What drip rate is required?
questions.questionZh: 需要用 10 gtts/mL 的输液器在 20 分钟内给一名 15 kg 儿童输入 300 mL 液体冲击量。所需滴速是多少？

options.en: 50 gtts/min
options.zh: 50 gtts/min

options.en: 100 gtts/min
options.zh: 100 gtts/min

options.en: 150 gtts/min
options.zh: 150 gtts/min

options.en: 30 gtts/min
options.zh: 30 gtts/min

questions.explanationEn: 300 mL x 10 gtts/mL / 20 minutes = 3000 / 20 = 150 gtts/min (formula on p.39). 50 gtts/min comes from dividing by 60 minutes instead of 20; 100 gtts/min from dividing by 30 minutes; 30 gtts/min from leaving out the drop factor (300 / 10). A rate this fast - about 2-3 drops per second - means watching the bag and the child closely; 300 mL is the full 20 mL/kg bolus for a 15 kg child (p.54).
questions.explanationZh: 300 mL × 10 gtts/mL ÷ 20 分钟 = 3000 ÷ 20 = 150 gtts/min（公式见第 39 页）。50 是错除以 60 分钟；100 是错除以 30 分钟；30 是漏乘滴系数（300 ÷ 10）。这么快的滴速（约每秒 2–3 滴）意味着要紧盯液袋和患儿；300 mL 正是 15 kg 儿童 20 mL/kg 的完整冲击量（第 54 页）。

questions.questionEn: An 11-month-old with a cough has audible grunting on expiration, head bobbing with each breath, and intercostal retractions. His SpO2 is 91% and he is alert. What is your interpretation and priority?
questions.questionZh: 一名 11 个月大、咳嗽的婴儿，呼气时可听到呻吟，每次呼吸都伴点头样动作，并有肋间凹陷。SpO2 91%，神志清楚。你的判断和首要处置是什么？

options.en: Grunting is a normal infant sound and needs no specific action
options.zh: 呻吟是婴儿的正常发声，不需要特别处理

options.en: He is alert with an SpO2 over 90%, so oxygen is not yet indicated
options.zh: 他神志清楚、SpO2 高于 90%，暂不需要给氧

options.en: Head bobbing suggests a neurological rather than a respiratory problem
options.zh: 点头样动作提示神经系统问题而不是呼吸问题

options.en: Severe respiratory distress - give oxygen, keep him calm, transport promptly
options.zh: 重度呼吸窘迫——给氧、让他保持安静、尽快转运

questions.explanationEn: Grunting (exhaling against a partly closed glottis to keep the alveoli open) and head bobbing (using the neck muscles to breathe) are work-of-breathing signs in the PAT; Nancy describes both as markers of moderate to severe hypoxia. With intercostal retractions and an SpO2 of 91%, this infant is in severe respiratory distress. Respiratory distress is a BC oxygen indication (p.11), and agitation increases oxygen demand, so handle him gently and transport without delay. A is wrong because grunting is often mistaken for whimpering but signals lower-airway disease. B is wrong because alertness and an SpO2 just above 90% do not offset clear signs of distress; the BC target is 94% or higher. C is wrong because head bobbing is a form of retraction - a respiratory sign.
questions.explanationZh: 呻吟（grunting，在声门半闭时呼气以撑开肺泡）和点头样呼吸（用颈部肌肉辅助呼吸）都是儿科评估三角（PAT）中呼吸做功的表现，教材（Nancy）将两者都视为中重度缺氧的标志。再加上肋间凹陷和 SpO2 91%，这名婴儿处于重度呼吸窘迫。呼吸窘迫是 BC 的给氧指征（第 11 页），哭闹会增加耗氧，所以要轻柔操作、立即转运。A 错：呻吟常被误认为是哼哼，但它提示下呼吸道病变。B 错：神志清楚、SpO2 略高于 90% 抵消不了明显的窘迫体征，BC 的目标是 ≥ 94%。C 错：点头样呼吸是凹陷的一种，属于呼吸体征。

questions.questionEn: What compression rate and depth does the BC guideline specify for CPR on a 6-year-old?
questions.questionZh: BC 指南规定为 6 岁儿童做 CPR 时的按压频率和深度是多少？

options.en: 80-100 per minute, at a fixed depth of about 4 cm
options.zh: 每分钟 80–100 次，固定深度约 4 cm

options.en: 100-120 per minute, one-third to one-half of chest depth
options.zh: 每分钟 100–120 次，胸廓前后径的 1/3 至 1/2

options.en: 100-120 per minute, at a fixed depth of 5 to 6 cm
options.zh: 每分钟 100–120 次，固定深度 5–6 cm

options.en: 120-140 per minute, one-third of the chest depth
options.zh: 每分钟 120–140 次，胸廓前后径的 1/3

questions.explanationEn: For infants and children, BC (p.43) specifies 100-120 compressions per minute at a depth of one-third to one-half of the chest diameter. A is wrong on both rate and depth. C uses the correct rate but the adult depth of 5-6 cm, which is not proportioned to a child's chest. D is too fast. Allow full recoil after each compression and keep interruptions under 5 seconds (p.42).
questions.explanationZh: 对婴儿和儿童，BC 考纲（第 43 页）规定按压频率为每分钟 100–120 次，深度为胸廓前后径的 1/3 至 1/2。A 的频率和深度都不对。C 频率正确，但用的是成人 5–6 cm 的深度，没有按儿童胸廓比例调整。D 频率过快。每次按压后要让胸廓完全回弹，中断时间控制在 5 秒以内（第 42 页）。

questions.questionEn: A baby born 3 hours ago requires CPR. What compression-to-ventilation ratio applies, and what is the role of the AED?
questions.questionZh: 一名出生 3 小时的新生儿需要 CPR。应采用什么按压通气比？AED 起什么作用？

options.en: 15:2 with the AED applied as soon as available
options.zh: 15:2，AED 一旦可用立即使用

options.en: 30:2 with the AED applied after 2 minutes
options.zh: 30:2，2 分钟后使用 AED

options.en: 3:1, and no AED is used in the neonate
options.zh: 3:1，新生儿不使用 AED

options.en: 5:1 with child AED pads in an anterior/posterior configuration
options.zh: 5:1，使用儿科电极片按前后位放置

questions.explanationEn: For a neonate (up to 28 days) the ratio is 3:1 and no AED is used. The ventilation-heavy ratio reflects that neonatal arrest is almost always respiratory in origin; shockable rhythms are so rare in this group that the AED has no role.
questions.explanationZh: 新生儿（出生 28 天内）按压通气比为 3:1，且不使用 AED。以通气为主的比例反映新生儿骤停几乎都源于呼吸问题；该人群可电击心律极为罕见，AED 无用武之地。

questions.questionEn: You deliver a baby who is floppy, limp, and not breathing, with a heart rate of 80. What is your first step under the newborn guideline?
questions.questionZh: 你接生的新生儿全身松软、没有呼吸，心率 80 次/分。按新生儿复苏指南，第一步应做什么？

options.en: Dry, stimulate, and keep warm for 30 seconds, then reassess
options.zh: 擦干、刺激并保暖 30 秒，然后复查

options.en: Start chest compressions, because the heart rate is below 100
options.zh: 开始胸外按压，因为心率低于 100

options.en: Ventilate with a BVM on 100% oxygen for 30 seconds
options.zh: 用接 100% 氧气的球囊面罩通气 30 秒

options.en: Apply the AED with pediatric pads and analyze
options.zh: 贴上儿科电极片的 AED 并分析心律

questions.explanationEn: Step 1 of BC's newborn sequence (p.44) is to dry, stimulate, and keep the baby warm for 30 seconds. If the heart rate is still below 100 bpm, move to step 2 (BVM on room air for 30 seconds), then step 3 (BVM with 100% oxygen for 30 seconds); if the rate is still below 100 after step 3, start step 4 - compressions with ventilations and 100% oxygen until the heart rate is above 60 bpm. B is wrong because compressions come only after the ventilation steps. C skips straight to step 3. D is wrong because BC states no AED for neonates. Nancy's text differs: following neonatal resuscitation guidelines, it starts compressions only if the heart rate stays below 60 after 30 seconds of effective ventilation; for the BC exam, use the BC sequence.
questions.explanationZh: BC 新生儿复苏流程（第 44 页）第 1 步是擦干、刺激并保暖 30 秒。若心率仍低于 100 次/分，进入第 2 步（室内空气球囊面罩通气 30 秒），再到第 3 步（接 100% 氧气的球囊面罩通气 30 秒）；第 3 步后心率仍低于 100，则进入第 4 步——按压加通气并给 100% 氧气，直到心率高于 60 次/分。B 错：按压要在通气步骤之后。C 直接跳到了第 3 步。D 错：BC 规定新生儿不用 AED。教材（Nancy）写法不同：按新生儿复苏指南，有效通气 30 秒后心率仍低于 60 才开始按压；BC 考试按 BC 流程作答。

questions.questionEn: After 30 seconds of drying, stimulation, and warming, a newborn's heart rate is 88 bpm and he still is not breathing effectively. What is the next step?
questions.questionZh: 擦干、刺激、保暖 30 秒后，新生儿心率 88 次/分，仍然没有有效呼吸。下一步是什么？

options.en: Ventilate with a BVM on room air for 30 seconds, then reassess
options.zh: 用球囊面罩以室内空气通气 30 秒，然后复查

options.en: Begin chest compressions with ventilations at a 3:1 ratio
options.zh: 以 3:1 的比例开始按压加通气

options.en: Continue drying and stimulating for another 30 seconds
options.zh: 再继续擦干和刺激 30 秒

options.en: Attach 100% oxygen to the BVM immediately and ventilate
options.zh: 立即给球囊面罩接上 100% 氧气并通气

questions.explanationEn: Step 2 of BC's newborn sequence (p.44) is ventilation with a BVM on room air for 30 seconds. Only if the heart rate remains below 100 bpm do you move to step 3 and attach 100% oxygen, and only if it remains below 100 after that do you begin compressions, continuing until the heart rate is above 60 bpm. B is wrong because compressions come after both ventilation steps. C is wrong because step 1 is a single 30-second period; if it fails, you move on to ventilation. D is wrong because room air comes first and 100% oxygen is step 3. Effective ventilation, not oxygen concentration, is the key intervention at this stage.
questions.explanationZh: BC 新生儿复苏流程第 2 步（第 44 页）是用球囊面罩以室内空气通气 30 秒。只有心率仍低于 100 次/分，才进入第 3 步接上 100% 氧气；之后仍低于 100 才开始胸外按压，并持续到心率高于 60 次/分。B 错：按压要在两个通气步骤之后。C 错：第 1 步只做一轮 30 秒，无效就进入通气。D 错：先用室内空气，100% 氧气是第 3 步。这一阶段的关键是有效通气，而不是氧浓度。

questions.questionEn: You have completed 30 seconds of BVM ventilation with 100% oxygen on a newborn. His heart rate is now 50 bpm. What should you do, and what is your endpoint?
questions.questionZh: 你已用接 100% 氧气的球囊面罩为新生儿通气 30 秒，现在心率 50 次/分。你应该怎么做？终点是什么？

options.en: Continue ventilations alone and reassess in 2 minutes
options.zh: 只继续通气，2 分钟后复查

options.en: Apply the AED and analyze before starting compressions
options.zh: 先贴 AED 分析心律，再开始按压

options.en: Start compressions with ventilations and 100% O2 until HR is above 60
options.zh: 开始按压加通气并给 100% 氧气，直到心率高于 60

options.en: Start compressions until HR is above 100, then stop ventilating
options.zh: 开始按压直到心率高于 100，然后停止通气

questions.explanationEn: Step 4 of BC's newborn sequence (p.44) is chest compressions with ventilations and 100% oxygen until the heart rate is above 60 bpm; a heart rate of 50 after step 3 (below 100) moves you to it. A is wrong because ventilation alone has already failed and a 2-minute delay is far too long. B is wrong because BC states no AED for neonates. D is wrong on both counts: the compression endpoint is above 60 bpm, and ventilations must not stop in a newborn who needed resuscitation. Note the two thresholds: 100 bpm moves you through the steps, 60 bpm ends compressions. Nancy's text differs on the trigger - it starts compressions only when the rate stays below 60 after effective ventilation; for the BC exam, use the BC sequence.
questions.explanationZh: BC 新生儿复苏流程第 4 步（第 44 页）是按压加通气并给 100% 氧气，直到心率高于 60 次/分；第 3 步后心率 50（低于 100），应进入这一步。A 错：单纯通气已经无效，再等 2 分钟太久。B 错：BC 规定新生儿不用 AED。D 两处都错：停止按压的终点是心率高于 60，而且需要复苏的新生儿不能停止通气。注意两个阈值：100 次/分决定是否进入下一步，60 次/分是停止按压的终点。教材（Nancy）写法不同：有效通气后心率仍低于 60 才开始按压；BC 考试按 BC 流程作答。

questions.questionEn: A 3-week-old is brought to you limp, mottled, and hypothermic, with a heart rate of 55 and shallow irregular respirations. Which management set is correct?
questions.questionZh: 一名 3 周大的婴儿被抱来时全身松软、皮肤花斑、体温偏低，心率 55 次/分，呼吸浅而不规则。哪一组处置正确？

options.en: Apply the AED first, since the bradycardia may be a shockable rhythm
options.zh: 先贴 AED——心动过缓可能是可电击心律

options.en: Use 15:2 with two rescuers, since he is older than 2 weeks
options.zh: 双人施救用 15:2——他已经超过 2 周大

options.en: Give oxygen only and wait until the heart rate falls below 40
options.zh: 只给氧，等心率降到 40 以下再按压

options.en: Ventilate and compress at 3:1 with no AED, keep him warm, and transport
options.zh: 以 3:1 通气加按压、不用 AED，注意保暖并转运

questions.explanationEn: At 21 days he is still within BC's neonatal definition (up to 28 days, p.44), so the 3:1 ratio applies and no AED is used. A heart rate below 60 with poor perfusion - limp and mottled - is an indication to start CPR (p.41), and warming matters because hypothermia both causes and worsens neonatal deterioration. A is wrong because BC uses no AED in neonates. B is wrong because 15:2 is for infants and children beyond 28 days. C is wrong because the trigger is a rate below 60 with poor perfusion; waiting for 40 lets him arrest.
questions.explanationZh: 21 天大仍在 BC 新生儿的定义范围内（出生 28 天以内，第 44 页），所以适用 3:1 比例、不用 AED。心率低于 60 且灌注不良（全身松软、花斑）就是开始 CPR 的指征（第 41 页）；保暖也很重要，因为低体温既会导致也会加重新生儿病情恶化。A 错：BC 规定新生儿不用 AED。B 错：15:2 用于超过 28 天的婴儿和儿童。C 错：开始按压的标准是心率低于 60 且灌注不良，等到 40 只会让他骤停。

questions.questionEn: You assist a delivery. After drying and stimulation the baby cries vigorously, has good tone, and her heart rate is 140. What is your management?
questions.questionZh: 你协助了一次分娩。擦干和刺激后，婴儿大声啼哭、肌张力良好，心率 140 次/分。你的处置是什么？

options.en: Give 30 seconds of room-air BVM ventilation as a precaution
options.zh: 保险起见，先用室内空气球囊面罩通气 30 秒

options.en: No resuscitation needed - keep her warm and dry and keep watching her
options.zh: 不需要复苏——保持温暖干燥，持续观察

options.en: Start compressions at 3:1, since all newborns need initial support
options.zh: 以 3:1 开始按压——所有新生儿都需要初始支持

options.en: Apply the AED to obtain a baseline rhythm for the hospital
options.zh: 贴 AED，为医院取得基线心律

questions.explanationEn: BC's newborn sequence (p.44) is triggered by a baby who is floppy, limp, not breathing, or has a heart rate below 100 bpm. A vigorous, crying baby with good tone and a heart rate of 140 meets none of these, so she needs warmth, drying, ongoing observation of breathing, tone, and heart rate, and transport with her mother. A is wrong because ventilation is for a newborn who is not breathing or whose heart rate stays below 100 after step 1. C is wrong because compressions on a baby with a rate of 140 cause harm. D is wrong because BC uses no AED in neonates.
questions.explanationZh: BC 新生儿复苏流程（第 44 页）的启动条件是：全身松软、无呼吸，或心率低于 100 次/分。大声啼哭、肌张力好、心率 140 的婴儿一项都不符合，因此只需保暖、擦干，持续观察呼吸、肌张力和心率，并与母亲一同转运。A 错：通气是给无呼吸或第 1 步后心率仍低于 100 的新生儿的。C 错：给心率 140 的婴儿按压会造成伤害。D 错：BC 规定新生儿不用 AED。
